item.title: Cavaliers' Mario Hezonja shines on Croatian Heritage Night vs. Pacers
item.description: CLEVELAND — A glimpse of Europe was in the stands Nov. 20 for Croatian Heritage Night as the Cavaliers took on the Indiana Pacers . "It means so much for us to get this opportunity for our Croatian community, to come together," a Croatian fan told the Beacon Journal. Nearly 400 Croatian fans sat pregame to watch Cavs forward Mario Hezonja and Pacers center Ivica Zubac, who are Croatia natives. Hezonja was able to talk to fans before he warmed up, then thanked them for coming out and sat with them for a group photo. "It means a lot if they're happy," Hezonja said after collecting 10 points and 10 rebounds in 20 minutes of the bench to help the Cavs beat the Pacers 128-119 on a night James Harden poured in 51 points. "They have somebody that is fighting for them on a court, that type of stuff. We are from a very small country, so it's super, super proud that I have that much support from the community like this." Cleveland is still fairly new for Hezonja, so being able to have a taste of home before a game meant a lot to him. “First of all, big congratulations and big thank you to my team, organization, the whole organization to getting this done," he said. "It's not easy having a brand-new player that just got back after six years, who’s Croatian, and then to organize something like this is huge. "I was also shocked by the number of how many people showed up. I know for sure some of the people couldn't make it, which I'm sad about it, so I want everybody to be together for these types of night, to be here.” Many fans felt the appreciation, too. They were given scarves and were wearing jerseys from their national soccer team. Some were even dressed in traditional clothing from Croatia. "Both my parents are straight off the boat — they came in the late '60s — we're here, first generation do a little bit of both old and new country," another fan said. "I'm trying to make sure [daughter] Emma is a part of that because it's very important for her to embrace the culture." Mario Hezonja's impact on the Cavaliers Hezonja was a lottery pick in the 2015 NBA draft, selected No. 5 overall by the Orlando Magic. After bouncing around the league, he left the NBA after six years to return to Europe, playing in Greece, Russia and Spain. The one-year, $2.8 million contract Hezonja signed over the summer became fully guaranteed on Nov. 15. Cavs general manager Koby Altman and coach Kenny Atkinson saw what Hezonja brings to the team and his impact early on. "Thank you, Koby, thank you organization and thanks to my teammates," Hezonja said. "They've been the ones that trust me. Thanks, Kenny and the coaching staff. They've been huge, huge help with me. My NBA career is in their hands. "I'm trying to help the best way I can. Today was the double-double. The next day is going to be something else. I'm an open book, open-minded about everything, so keep doing it.” With his playing time increasing, Hezonja has upped his averages to 9.1 points, 5.4 rebounds and 1.8 assists

item.title: Jordan Stolz nears becoming youngest speed skater to reach 50 World Cup wins
item.description: Jordan Stolz, after an offseason of change , opened the post-Olympic season with podium finishes in his first three races, including his 48th career World Cup win. Stolz, a 22-year-old who won two golds and one silver at the Milan Cortina Olympics, claimed the 500m in a track record in Obihiro, Japan, on Saturday. About 90 minutes later, he took second in the 1500m, 21 hundredths behind Ning Zhongyan of China, who also relegated Stolz to runner-up in that event at the Milan Cortina Olympics. Earlier on Friday, Stolz was third in the 1000m in Obihiro, snapping a 14-race World Cup win streak at that distance dating to 2023 (counting A division races only). The last time Stolz was beaten in a World Cup 1000m was Nov. 10, 2023, when he finished third in that season's opener in Obihiro. He owns the 1000m world record of 1:05.37 set in Kearns, Utah, on Jan. 26, 2024. Stolz is slated to race another 500m in Obihiro on the last day of the stop on Sunday, live on Peacock . Stolz is two wins from becoming the youngest speed skater — by nearly five years — to reach 50 individual World Cup victories, according to Speedskatingstats.com. Jeremy Wotherspoon of Canada, a sprint star in the 1990s and 2000s, is currently the youngest to do so — at age 27. Stolz would be one of the youngest athletes across all winter sports to reach that milestone. Younger than Alpine skier Mikaela Shiffrin (who was 23 years old in 2018) and Norwegian cross-country skier Johannes Høsflot Klæbo (who was 26 in 2022). Japanese ski jumper Sara Takanashi did it younger at age 20 in 2017. The only male speed skaters with more individual World Cup wins are Wotherspoon (67) and American Shani Davis (58), who advises Stolz. The overall record holder in speed skating is German Gunda Niemann, who won 98 times. After Obihiro, Stolz can target 50 at the next World Cup in Heerenveen, Netherlands, from Dec. 4-6. Heerenveen's famed Thialf arena will host speed skating at the 2030 Alps Winter Olympics. For Jordan Stolz, some changes and one constant under his pillow to start post-Olympic season Jordan Stolz returns to World Cup speed skating competition, live on Peacock. Nick Zaccardi ,

item.title: What's the Browns AFC playoff competition? A look at the contenders
item.description: BEREA ― The Browns are in the playoff hunt . That is not a typo. Cleveland is 6-4 and in the No. 7 spot in the AFC playoff standings heading into Nov. 22 games. The Browns are on their bye for Week 11, which got started with the Houston Texans pounding the Indianapolis Colts 26-3 on "Thursday Night Football." What happens over the next eight weeks will be fascinating to watch play out, especially once the Browns rejoin the fun with a "Sunday Night Football" appearance against the Las Vegas Raiders on Nov. 29. It'll be all about handling the pressure, and proving the six wins weren't the byproduct of a whole lot of luck. Subscribe to Browns Insider newsletter So what does the AFC playoff picture look like, at least around the area where the Browns reside? Let's dive into the teams around the Browns, starting with the AFC North leaders. Cincinnati Bengals (7-2) Current position: No. 4/AFC North leaders AFC record: 5-2 AFC North record: 2-1 Against Cleveland this season: 0-0, play twice in final six games QB situation: Joe Burrow is on an MVP-like heater. Remaining schedule: vs. New Orleans Saints at Cleveland Browns vs. Kansas City Chiefs at Carolina Panthers at Indianapolis Colts vs. Baltimore Ravens vs. Cleveland Browns Playoff vibes: This might be the best team in the AFC when it's all said and done. The schedule has a couple of big games remaining, but nothing too daunting. They're really just on here because of the AFC North race, which they could take a huge step in wrapping up with a win over the Browns in a couple of weeks. Or, if they were to lose, opening the door for an interesting finish. Denver Broncos (7-2) Current position: No. 5/First AFC wild card AFC record: 3-1 Against Cleveland this season: Nothing to see here, because they don't play. QB situation: It's Bo Nix, so your mileage may vary. Remaining schedule: vs. Las Vegas Raiders at Pittsburgh Steelers vs. Miami Dolphins at New York Jets at Las Vegas Raiders vs. Buffalo Bills at New England Patriots vs. Los Angeles Chargers Playoff vibes: That schedules aligns perfectly for the Broncos to not only stay comfortably in the playoff mix, but maybe even overtake the Chiefs for the AFC West title. Pittsburgh Steelers (6-3) Current position: No. 6/Second AFC wild card AFC record: 3- 3 AFC North record: 2-2 Against Cleveland this season: 1-1, lost in Cleveland 27-24 in Week 4, won in Pittsburgh 27-3 in Week 8 QB situation: Aaron Rodgers, but Aaron Rodgers 2026 version, so it's all dependent on the day. Remaining schedule: at Philadelphia Eagles vs. Denver Broncos vs. Houston Texans at Jacksonville Jaguars vs. Buffalo Bills vs. Carolina Panthers vs. Tennessee Titans at Baltimore Ravens Playoff vibes: It might be the toughest remaining schedule on paper of those residing in this part of the AFC playoff picture. The good news for them is they're done with the Bengals. The bad news for them is they look like almost every other Steelers team the last nine or 10 years, which means about nine or 10 wins and nothing once they get to the playoffs Cleveland Browns (6-4) Current position: No. 7/Seventh AFC wild card AFC record: 4-3 AFC North record: 2-1 QB situation: Depends on if it's the first three quarters or the final quarter. Even then, are there 10 minutes remaining or are there two minutes left? That's the Deshaun Watson experience in 2026. Remaining schedule: Bye week vs. Las Vegas Raiders vs. Cincinnati Bengals vs. Atlanta Falcons at New York Giants at Baltimore Ravens vs. Indianapolis Colts at Cincinnati Bengals Playoff vibes: They should be feeling pretty good, although it's Cleveland, so feeling good is a very subjective thing. The schedule is set up with some winnable games left, including two of the remaining three on the four-game homestand they're in the midst of. New England Patriots (5-5) Current position: No. 8/First one out of AFC wild card AFC record: 5-1 Against Cleveland this season: Didn't play in a game that actually counts in the standings. QB situation: Drake Maye may very well be done for the season. Tommy DeVito? Maybe? Daniel Jones now that he's available? Could be. Remaining schedule: Bye week at Los Angeles Chargers vs. Buffalo Bills vs. Minnesota Vikings at Kansas City Chiefs at New York Jets vs. Denver Broncos vs. Miami Dolphins Playoff vibes: The combination of quarterback injury and brutal schedule in the middle of the stretch run makes it hard to imagine the Patriots can stay in the race to the bitter end. Houston Texans (4-6) Current position: No. 9/Second out in AFC race AFC record: 4-4 Against Cleveland this season: Lost 27-24 in Week 10 in a game that looms large in the playoff race. QB situation: C.J. Stroud has been playing really well of late. Except when the Browns blitzed him relentlessly over the final three quarters of a Week 10 game. Remaining schedule: vs. Baltimore Ravens at Pittsburgh Steelers at Washington Commanders vs. Jacksonville Jaguars at Philadelphia Eagles at Green Bay Packers vs. Tennessee Titans Playoff vibes: Pointing upward again after the loss to the Browns. However, that loss to the Browns may be the reason why the Texans don't have a path to the playoffs. That, and some tricky games still remaining. Las Vegas Raiders (4-6) Current position: No. 10/Third team out in AFC race AFC record: 3- 3 Against Cleveland this season: 0-0, but playing them in Week 12 on "Sunday Night Football" QB situation: "There was something in the air that night/The stars were bright, Fernando/They were shining there for you and me/For liberty, Fernando/Though I never thought that we could lose/There's no regret/If I had to do the same again/I would, my friend, Fernando" ― ABBA, but probably also Mark Davis, Tom Brady, Klint Kubiak and the rest of the Raiders decision-makers about No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza, who became the starter when Kirk Cousins was traded at the deadline. Remaining schedule: at Denver Broncos at Cleveland Browns Bye week vs. Los Angeles Chargers vs. Denver Broncos vs. Tennessee Titans at Arizona Cardinals at Kansas City Chiefs Playoff vibes: The Raiders have signaled their intentions by shifting to Mendoza. However, the next two games before their bye probably will make or break any lingering playoff hopes. Baltimore Ravens (4-6) Current position: No. 11/Fifth out in AFC race AFC record: 2-5 AFC North record: 0-2 Against Cleveland this season: 0-1, lost 13-10 in Week 7 in Cleveland, and still have to play in Baltimore in Week 16 QB situation: Lamar Jackson's hurt and so is Tyler Huntley. They've brought in Jacoby Brissett to try to keep them afloat. item.title: James Harden boosts Cavaliers with memorable 51-point game vs. Pacers
item.description: CLEVELAND — Cavaliers point guard James Harden dribbled with his left hand as he drove to the basket against Indiana guard Quenton Jackson, maneuvered between Jackson and Pacers center Jay Huff and then used his right hand to make a layup as time expired in the third quarter. The left-handed shooting Harden was immediately greeted by Cavaliers teammates who were in awe of the move and his scoring outburst. Wing Peyton Watson yelled in Harden's face with unbridled enthusiasm, and guard Donovan Mitchell placed both of his hands atop his head as if his mind had been blown. "I think that's the joy that we have to bring for each other on a night-to-night basis, even when things aren't going well," Harden said. "The excitement that we have for each other is contagious." The Cavs reveled in a memorable night for Harden, who scored a game-high 51 points in their 128-119 victory over the Indiana Pacers on Friday, Nov. 20, at Rocket Arena. By triumphing in an NBA Cup Game, the Cavs (9-8) improved to 2-1 in East Group B. The 37-year-old Harden played as if he had borrowed the Cup during pregame warm-ups, dipped it in the fountain of youth and chugged. "Vintage performance — very reminiscent of his Houston days," Cavs coach Kenny Atkinson said of Harden, who won the 2017-18 NBA Most Valuable Player award with the Rockets. Harden passed the late Kobe Bryant for the third-most 50-point games in NBA history with 26. Only Wilt Chamberlain (118) and Michael Jordan (31) have more. "Obviously, Wilt was elite, but you've got Mike and Kobe, [at the] shooting guard position, they were just the best to ever do it," Harden said. "So, just to be in that conversation, it's very humbling, and it's definitely special." Harden said he thought he could have a prolific scoring night "from the jump." He wound up with his highest point total since the Cavs acquired him this past February in a trade that sent point guard Darius Garland to the Los Angeles Clippers. Harden scored 15 points in the first quarter, nine in the second, 18 in the third and nine in the fourth, when he accounted for seven of Cleveland's final nine points to ensure a rally by Indiana (5-11) would fall short. Cavs news: Cavaliers vs Pacers highlights, stats, injury news, lineups and more Harden was efficient, too. He finished 15-of-26 shooting from the floor (57.7%), including 7 of 11 on 3-pointers (63.6%). He made all 14 of his free throws. He also compiled six rebounds, a team-high six assists against just two turnovers and one steal in 40 minutes. "This is history. These individual accomplishments in this league, people value that because it's extremely hard to do," said Cavs forward Mario Hezonja, who hails from Croatia and spent the past six seasons playing in Europe. "I come from a culture that doesn't look at that, and I kind of get mad at it because, hey, you have to cherish individual talent as well because individual talent gets you to the top. So, I'm so happy to be here to see these things again

He wound up with his highest point total since the Cavs acquired him this past February in a trade that sent point guard Darius Garland to the Los Angeles Clippers. Cavs news: Cavaliers vs Pacers highlights, stats, injury news, lineups and more Harden was efficient, too. He finished 15-of-26 shooting from the floor (57.7%), including 7 of 11 on 3-pointers (63.6%). He made all 14 of his free throws. He also compiled six rebounds, a team-high six assists against just two turnovers and one steal in 40 minutes. "This is history. These individual accomplishments in this league, people value that because it's extremely hard to do," said Cavs forward Mario Hezonja, who hails from Croatia and spent the past six seasons playing in Europe. "I come from a culture that doesn't look at that, and I kind of get mad at it because, hey, you have to cherish individual talent as well because individual talent gets you to the top. So, I'm so happy to be here to see these things again and see them live. It's like the essence of basketball." Although Harden has produced other bright spots this season, including 32 points in the Cavs' 115-107 win at the defending NBA champion New York Knicks on Nov. 11, the 11-time All-Star has also been a popular target of criticism. His defensive deficiencies are not a secret, but the question is whether he can play well enough on offense to compensate for them. He certainly did against the Pacers, becoming the sixth player in NBA history 37 or older to record a 50-point game. "It's easy when you're young, 23, 24, you run around, you jump high and can move fast and get by people," Harden said. "Now it's like, OK, you're not as fast. Can you still get by people? Or how can you get by somebody? "That's the evolution of James Harden, figuring that out. If I can master that or get to a really good space in that point, man, I'm still going to be elite. That's where I am. Tonight was a confidence booster that I can do it at a high level still." Cavs news: First Nicaraguan NBA player Norchad Omier is one to watch with Cleveland Cavaliers Harden was asked whether he doubted he could still do it, even though he scored 55 points on Nov. 22, 2025, as a member of the Clippers. While Harden fielded the question in the Cavs locker room, Mitchell walked behind the scrum of reporters surrounding his teammate and chimed in by saying "y'all did" doubt Harden could do it. Later, Mitchell said, "I'm glad he had a night like this tonight because I felt like a lot of people were getting on him a little bit. And I think that's one way to answer it. Do we expect it every night? No, but if he does it, great. But I think the biggest thing is to see him in that form — aggressive. You're looking at one of the greatest players of all time. It's definitely good to see, amazing to see." Atkinson said Harden is "just getting into form, getting into better shape" lately. Atkinson explained Harden's contractual situation this past summer kept him from sticking to his typical offseason routine filled with pickup basketball. He re-signed with the Cavs for three years and $97 million, yet the two sides waited for other moves to materialize first and didn't agree to the deal until Aug. 20. The delay gave the team financial flexibility, aiding its sign-and-trade move for Watson. "After that, I started to ramp up, ramp up, ramp up," Harden said. "So, all in all, the first 15, 17 games we've been in, things haven't been going the best for me personally, but I think it's bigger than me, and I think it's about our team. Getting guys back healthy is important, and we'll figure it out." Harden figured it out at a good time because Mitchell said he was "sick as a dog" against the Pacers, who, like the Cavs, have used nine different starting lineups this season. Even at less than full strength, Mitchell scored 20 points on 8-of-17 shooting from the field (2 of 7 on 3s) before sipping bone broth after the game. Now Harden and Mitchell are among the six players in Cavs history to reach at least 50 points in a single outing. Mitchell scored 71 points on Jan. 2, 2023. "We won't [appreciate Harden's career enough] until it's over with," Mitchell said. "I hate it, but that's just the world we live in. We won't appreciate greatness. We didn't appreciate Russ [Russell Westbrook] in his latter years until now it's like, 'Oh, man, Russ was this and that.' "I hate that it takes a monumental performance for us to be like, 'Oh, yeah, [Harden is] pretty good.' But credit to him, man. He's worked his butt off. I've been around it my whole career. It's just a level of consistency that we all respect and appreciate in this locker room." And with inconsistency defining the 2026-27 Cavs thus far, the buzz Harden created for the entire team was desperately needed. Nate Ulrich is the sports columnist of the Akron Beacon Journal and a sports features writer. Nate can be reached at nulrich@thebeaconjournal.com . On Twitter: @ByNateUlrich . item.title: What happened when Juventus last beat Venezia?
item.description: What happened when Juventus last beat Venezia? The Men’s First Team are back in Serie A action after the international break, this time taking on Venezia at the Allianz Stadium in the 12:30 CET slot on Sunday, November 22. The Bianconeri are currently pushing to get into the European places, whilst Venezia sit in the relegation zone and will be hoping to cause an upset. Let’s take a look at the last time Juventus beat Venezia. Champions League football secured Venezia have bounced between Serie A and Serie B frequently in recent years, meaning the last clash between the Arancioneroverdi and the Bianconeri came in May 2025. It proved to be an incredibly important one for both teams, with Juventus clinching a Champions League place and Venezia being relegated. The match at the Stadio Pier Luigi Penzo began in dramatic fashion, with Daniel Fila putting Venezia ahead after just two minutes. It seemed that just two minutes later, Juventus had equalised, but Alberto Costa’s excellent strike was ruled out for a handball. It took another 20 minutes before the equaliser did come. Kenan Yildiz charged at the Venezia defence and they gave him enough space to get a shot on target, which went underneath Andrei Radu. In a flash, Juventus had turned the game around. The ball broke on the edge of the box for Randal Kolo Muani, who charged into the box and fired past Radu, making it 2-1 to the Bianconeri. Despite falling behind, Eusebio Di Francesco’s side rallied in the second half and soon found an equaliser, with Ridgeciano Haps scoring and making it 2-2. Just after Michele Di Gregorio produced a fine save to keep the score level, Francisco Conceicao won a penalty thanks to his quick feet. Manuel Locatelli stepped up and scored, putting Juventus back in control. There were contrasting scenes at full-time, as Igor Tudor’s side celebrated Champions League qualification, and Venezia’s players and fans came to terms with relegation. View this post on YouTube

item.title: Kane vows to be back for ‘business end of the season’ after surgery
item.description: Bayern Munich's Harry Kane (L) receives treatment for an injury during the German Bundesliga soccer match between Bayern Munich and Cologne at Allianz Arena. (is associated with: «Kane vows to be back for ‘business end of the season’ after surgery») Tom Weller/dpa Harry Kane is targeting the “business end of the season” after undergoing surgery on a torn ligament in his left ankle. Bayern Munich said the operation on the injury, sustained in Friday’s 1-1 draw with Cologne, was a success but the 33-year-old is expected to be out for months as a result. Kane wrote on Instagram: “The highs and lows of life! Obviously very disappointed to get this injury but as always it’s an opportunity to show resilience and improvement going into 2027. “I’ll be back fresh and ready to go for the business end of the season! “Tough times don’t last, tough people do” – my guy @edelman11 (Julian Edelman, three-time Super Bowl winner with the New England Patriots) told me this one! “Thank you for all the messages! Alles gut.” The end of the message is German for "Everything’s fine." Kane sustained the injury when he was scythed down in the area by Cologne defender Joel Schmied, who reached Michael Olise’s low cross first but clattered into the Ballon d’Or winner’s left leg in his follow-through at the back post. The England captain writhed in pain and, although he gingerly got back to his feet and initially soldiered on, it was clear he could not continue and he hobbled off the field alongside two physios after treatment. After the match Bayern confirmed Kane had torn the syndesmotic ligament and “will therefore be sidelined for the next few months”. Kane earlier this month signed a new deal with the Bundesliga giants until June 2029 – reportedly worth in excess of £400,000 ($517,600) a week, making him the highest-paid player in Europe before bonuses. Since arriving from Tottenham three years ago, Kane has bagged a scarcely believable 156 goals in 163 appearances in all competitions, helping Bayern win a league and cup double last season. He went into the international break having a drawn a blank in his four previous matches for Bayern but he scored twice for England, including from the spot in their 3-2 Nations League win over Spain. But after being forced off after 20 minutes at the Allianz Arena, replaced by Tom Bischof, Kane could now be facing a battle to be fully fit for England’s two-legged quarter-final against Norway in March.

item.title: Hutch should take a page from Barry Sanders, avoid injury | Letters
item.description: Hutch, we needed you on the field I grew up watching the Lions on black and white TV in the days of Milt Plum, Lem Barney, Joe Schmidt, Dick "Night Train" Lane and Tommy Watkins. I have been a Detroit Lions fan since the early 1960s, and I have seen the NFL change for the good and for the not so good. The thing that bothers me greatly is how today's players make everything about them, not the team. In this modern era of the NFL, there is one player who was the consummate pro in how he conducted himself on the field of play, and that was Barry Sanders. After one of his spectacular runs or touchdowns, he didn't run and chest bump a teammate, he didn't spike the ball, he didn't run and jump into the stands, he just handed the ball to the referee. I'm saying all of this to address Aidan Hutchinson's injury, that was avoidable! He wasn't hurt on a play, he was hurt celebrating a sack, something he gets paid to do, something he is supposed to do. Because of his actions, he is lost for the season as the Lions make a playoff run, and his season is over. More importantly, he has let his team down. As a star player at his position, he needs to understand his importance to the team and act accordingly. Today's players make what they do about them, look at me, see what I did. Just do your job and let that speak for itself, like Barry did. High five a teammate, don't put more stress on your body than the game already does. I recall some years ago another Lion did the same thing and was lost for the season due to injury. Hutch, we need you on the field, not on crutches. In the words of Bo Schembechler, "The Team, The Team, The Team!" James J. Smith Battle Creek Bills fan will root for Lions on Thanksgiving Day During the war, my father was stationed at Selfridge Field. The Detroit Lions let military attend games for free. My father would buy a ticket for my mother, take her to her seat, go to the seats allotted to the military, and after the game started, go and sit with my mother. I was born after the war, and can remember not having a television as a child. When we finally got a television, one of the two channels carried the Lions' Thanksgiving Day game. Since that game, I have missed only one game. In 1969, I was in basic training, and while there was no training scheduled on Thanksgiving Day, I was caught reading a newspaper and was given extra duty, and I missed that game. The first time I saw the Lions play live was the last game played at War Memorial Stadium in Buffalo. It was a 21-21 tie. The next year, the Bills moved into the Ralph. I am an unapologetic, loud, proud Bills fan, but for a couple of hours on Thanksgiving Day, I will be a loud proud Lions fan. Let’s go, Lions. Theodore E. In the words of Bo Schembechler, "The Team, The Team, The Team!" James J. Smith Battle Creek Bills fan will root for Lions on Thanksgiving Day During the war, my father was stationed at Selfridge Field. The Detroit Lions let military attend games for free. My father would buy a ticket for my mother, take her to her seat, go to the seats allotted to the military, and after the game started, go and sit with my mother. I was born after the war, and can remember not having a television as a child. When we finally got a television, one of the two channels carried the Lions' Thanksgiving Day game. In 1969, I was in basic training, and while there was no training scheduled on Thanksgiving Day, I was caught reading a newspaper and was given extra duty, and I missed that game. I am an unapologetic, loud, proud Bills fan, but for a couple of hours on Thanksgiving Day, I will be a loud proud Lions fan. Let’s go, Lions. Theodore E. Boesel Rochester, New York Dan Campbell is to blame for Lions discipline problems The Detroit Lions have chronic team discipline problems, and the responsibility for it sits with the coach. I have a hard time believing Brad Holmes, when he drafted this team, had the foresight to see some of the incredible, non-football nonsense that happens in these games. And the referees see it. How many penalties will it take before one finally sees the same old, same old Lions? Dan Holden Essexville, Michigan There's a long history of Black cowboys Jordan Williams follows a long tradition of Black cowboys and lawmen in both history and local popular culture. (" Why did 2 horses board a Detroit bus? See footage, hear from owner ," Detroit Free Press, Nov. 13.) The number of Black U.S. deputy marshals sworn by Judge Isaac Parker to serve in Indian Territory was disproportionate to numbers in the regional population, and one such deputy marshal, Bass Reeves, was most probably the model for The Lone Ranger, which originated on Detroit radio station WXYZ in 1933. Harry Frank Ann Arbor Albom's selective outrage at cruel humor Mitch Albom is right. Laughing at someone's murder is not funny. (" Mitch Albom: Laughing at Kirk's murder only shows how low we have sunk ," Detroit Free Press, Nov. 15.) I do not recall reading a similar editorial when the president himself mocked a brutal attack on Paul Pelosi , and when his son created a meme about a Halloween costume mocking the Pelosi attack. That was not funny either. Also not funny was slamming Robert Mueller's death , slamming John McCain's capture , and so much more that comes out of the White House. Let's put the blame for lowered standards where it belongs. Mocking a disabled reporter in 2015 should have derailed Donald Trump's election immediately, Instead, it started the country down a path of cruelty as humor. The president is supposed to set an example. What does one expect as the American people follow the example of the grotesque and cruel "humor" constantly demonstrated by the leader of the country? You reap what you sow. Roxanne Lopetrone Garden City The RenCen plans look great I, my wife and my children were born in Detroit. I'm retired, but my international law firm is still headquartered in Detroit. I lived in Detroit for much of my career. I am 85, and have been a Detroit fan longer than many of the critics of the RenCen deal outlined by the recent Jamaine Dickens editorial have been alive. (" The RenCen deal costs Detroiters nothing. Rejecting it will ," Detroit Free Press, Nov. 11.) I have watched with dismay the negative attitudes of the harsh critics of the proposal to open up a plaza on the Detroit River and rehab the RenCen. Frankly, the plans look great and this project will save one of the most dominant features on the Detroit skyline from becoming a symbol of decay and decline. It is incredible that it is being criticized by people who have no money on the line. I am reminded of many MAGAs: "I'll believe what I want to believe; spare me the facts." Despite my last name, I am (unfortunately) not related to him, and have never met the man. But in my view, he was one of the primary saviors of Detroit when it was an international symbol of urban decay. I lived and worked in Detroit during those times, and have a memory. It is appalling that, according to Dickens, he has some vociferous critics now. Bob Gilbert Leland Submit a letter to the editor at freep.com/letters , and we may publish it in print and online. item.title: The Lazio Paradox: Off to Best Season Start Ever as Fans Boycott Home Fixtures
item.description: The Lazio Paradox: Off to Best Season Start Ever as Fans Boycott Home Fixtures Oftentimes in football, success on the pitch can mask cracks beneath the surface and provide cover for mismanagement. That’s not the case for the current Serie A leaders, Lazio, who are at the league’s summit after 11 matches yet dead last in attendance. The best start to a season in club history has been marred by an ongoing fan protest against owner Claudio Lotito, as their unbeaten run—including five wins and one draw at home—has coincided with an average attendance of just 10,141. The cavernous and once daunting Stadio Olimpico regresses to an awkward, echoey stage for the club’s brilliance on the pitch. An open letter published in January laid out many of the fans’ concerns, namely a lack of investment resulting in a stagnant period for the club, along with transfer restrictions and Lotito’s various other ventures pulling his attention away from the Biancocelesti . But they show up in droves to away matches, making it clear that their passion hasn’t wavered, just their faith in the man pulling the strings. And the supporters’ commitment to the boycott of home fixtures is made even more impressive by the fact that Lazio’s 29 points are their highest-ever total through 11 games. They boast the league’s best defense, conceding just nine goals, and their 25 goals scored are the third most in the division. Though it’s still early in the campaign, this breakneck start came almost out of nowhere. Gennaro Gattuso took over in the dugout at a time when his managerial stock was undeniably low after failing to qualify for the World Cup with Italy. The squad he inherited finished ninth last term and saw many key players depart over the summer. Some shrewd reinforcements did come, most notably midfielder Davide Frattesi who scored in each of his first three games with the club, but not to a degree which should have precipitated this early success. And yet, Gattuso has made this side more than the sum of its parts, as Frattesi is one of three players with four goals to lead an attack that has seen 12 different goalscorers. The staunchest back line in the league thus far has been anchored by Oliver Provstgaard, who few would have predicted to show such consistency after serving largely as a reserve last year. He’s been partnered by both Josip Sutalo, on loan from Ajax, and Danilho Doekhi, who joined on a free transfer from Union Berlin. A pair of Lotito-esque, low-budget signings that didn’t turn heads when they joined but have exceeded expectations. Nuno Tavares is back close to his best at left back and the right flank has been dutifully manned by Romano Floriani Mussolini, the much-talked about great-grandson of Benito Mussolini who has let his stellar play do the talking. Gustav Isaksen and Tijjani Noslin join Frattesi as the joint top goal scorers, while Mattia Zaccagni has provided his usual consistency and leadership to round out the attack. item.content:encoded: The Lazio Paradox: Off to Best Season Start Ever as Fans Boycott Home Fixtures Oftentimes in football, success on the pitch can mask cracks beneath the surface and provide cover for mismanagement. That’s not the case for the current Serie A leaders, Lazio, who are at the league’s summit after 11 matches yet dead last in attendance. The best start to a season in club history has been marred by an ongoing fan protest against owner Claudio Lotito, as their unbeaten run—including five wins and one draw at home—has coincided with an average attendance of just 10,141. The cavernous and once daunting Stadio Olimpico regresses to an awkward, echoey stage for the club’s brilliance on the pitch. An open letter published in January laid out many of the fans’ concerns, namely a lack of investment resulting in a stagnant period for the club, along with transfer restrictions and Lotito’s various other ventures pulling his attention away from the Biancocelesti . But they show up in droves to away matches, making it clear that their passion hasn’t wavered, just their faith in the man pulling the strings. And the supporters’ commitment to the boycott of home fixtures is made even more impressive by the fact that Lazio’s 29 points are their highest-ever total through 11 games. They boast the league’s best defense, conceding just nine goals, and their 25 goals scored are the third most in the division. Though it’s still early in the campaign, this breakneck start came almost out of nowhere. Gennaro Gattuso took over in the dugout at a time when his managerial stock was undeniably low after failing to qualify for the World Cup with Italy. The squad he inherited finished ninth last term and saw many key players depart over the summer. Some shrewd reinforcements did come, most notably midfielder Davide Frattesi who scored in each of his first three games with the club, but not to a degree which should have precipitated this early success. And yet, Gattuso has made this side more than the sum of its parts, as Frattesi is one of three players with four goals to lead an attack that has seen 12 different goalscorers. The staunchest back line in the league thus far has been anchored by Oliver Provstgaard, who few would have predicted to show such consistency after serving largely as a reserve last year. He’s been partnered by both Josip Sutalo, on loan from Ajax, and Danilho Doekhi, who joined on a free transfer from Union Berlin. A pair of Lotito-esque, low-budget signings that didn’t turn heads when they joined but have exceeded expectations. Nuno Tavares is back close to his best at left back and the right flank has been dutifully manned by Romano Floriani Mussolini, the much-talked about great-grandson of Benito Mussolini who has let his stellar play do the talking. Gustav Isaksen and Tijjani Noslin join Frattesi as the joint top goal scorers, while Mattia Zaccagni has provided his usual consistency and leadership to round out the attack. Reda Belahayne has flourished as the team’s regista , finally coming good after a January 2025 move from Hellas Verona. He’s filling in for the still-injured Nicolò Rovella, whose return will only bolster what’s been a formidable midfield to this point. Speaking of which, Kenneth Taylor has now fully settled after joining this past winter from Ajax and ties the side together between the lines. Gattuso’s approach received a bit of a refresh, too, as Lazio play intricate attacking football and mainly keep the ball on the ground as they progress fluidly up the pitch. Patterns of play are evident and a positional understanding between players has produced some fun-to-watch attacking moves. They’ve constructed the 5th-most attacks of 10-or-more passes in Serie A (166) and average the fourth-most passes per build-up sequence (4.23). Patience has been a virtue for the Biancocelesti , also ranking sixth in the league in average possession (53.7%). The staunch defense isn’t the result of a smothering press either, with Lazio preferring solidity and organization as they are near the bottom of Serie A in pressed sequences (99, 16th) and seventh in passes per defensive action (12.7). This means that they do employ pressure, but it’s calculated and not constant. It’s also helped that Christos Mandas is having a career year between the posts, keeping four clean sheets while his 5.88 goals prevented are second in the division. Despite all of the reasons for praise, there are still some concerns when it comes to the underlying numbers. Gattuso’s men have overperformed their expected goals by a whopping 7.66, and opponents have scored 4.62 less goals than expected. This suggests that the truth lies somewhere in between their league-leading actual figures and fairly pedestrian xG marks. Nonetheless, the Biancocelesti ’s next three fixtures after the international break are favorable on paper: at home to Lecce, away against Torino and back home versus a struggling Atalanta side. After that comes the derby against Roma, with their rivals also in the early title race, making for one of the highest-stakes clashes between the capital clubs in years. There’s a lot of season left and plenty of time for Lazio to stumble from their early pedestal. There are indications that this should happen, but they’ve already defied a lot of odds to be on top at this stage in the first place. The same can be said of the fans, who’ve proven their determination in defying Lotito long ago. Then the real question becomes, what will give first? A slide down the table or Lazio’s fans returning as they truly lock horns in a scudetto challenge come March? One of the most intriguing storylines in European football has plenty left to unfold as clubs resume this weekend. Stay tuned.

item.title: Bayern Munich considering Jamal Musiala sale after health problems
item.description: Bayern Munich are considering selling Jamal Musiala over concerns that his ongoing health problems will prevent him from returning to his best form. Musiala, 23, was diagnosed with a “neurological dysfunction” after suffering an on-pitch collapse twice in a matter of days during pre-season friendlies against Heidenheim and RB Leipzig. The Germany international said he was “very optimistic... there is no additional health risk beyond this” and indicated the condition would not hamper his highly promising career. However, Bayern chief Karl-Heinz Rummenigge has now admitted that the club are assessing his future amid a downturn in performances, publicly questioning whether the club can now justify his lofty salary. Rummenigge told Sky Germany : “He has a health-related issue. It's also well known that he has a contract involving very substantial sums of money. As a club, we have to consider how to deal with that situation. I think that's responsible and perfectly normal. “What we know unfortunately suggests it will be difficult for him to get back to the level he has often shown here in this stadium.” Musiala was reportedly Bayern’s best-paid player until Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane penned a contract extension earlier this month. He has been limited to just four appearances in the Bundesliga this term due to a muscle injury, scoring one goal and notching one assist, with fitness problems continuing to plague him after spending over half of last season out with a broken leg. Rummenigge says “a decision will have to be made” over his Musiala if he fails to show signs of improvement, but admitted that the former Chelsea academy product’s health issues would make a sale difficult. Rummenigge added: “We need to talk to the family, the player, and the agency, because then these sums of money, sorry, with all due respect, are no longer feasible. “I cannot imagine that Jamal wants to leave the club or that any other club would buy him under these conditions. “We are all interested in his return, ideally in top form. But what happens if that isn’t the case? Then we still have to think about the finances. “The discussion hasn’t taken place yet. These are just ideas at this stage.”

item.title: 'I'll be back': vows Kane after ankle surgery
item.description: Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane leaves the pitch with an ankle injury in Friday's Bundesliga match with Cologne. (Karl-Josef HILDENBRAND) Bayern Munich's star striker Harry Kane pledged to return for the "business end of the season" after undergoing surgery on his left ankle on Saturday. Kane limped off after 20 minutes of Bayern's 1-1 home draw with Cologne in their Bundesliga match on Friday, the club confirming the England captain had torn a ligament in his ankle. Bayern issued a statement Saturday saying the Ballon d'Or winner had "successfully undergone surgery" on his left ankle. "The 33-year-old will now begin his rehabilitation program," Bayern said, with the injury expected to keep Kane out for three to four months. Kane posted a picture on social media from his hospital bed on Saturday, vowing to work his way back to fitness this season. "The highs and lows of life! Obviously very disappointed to get this injury but as always it's an opportunity to show resilience and improvement going into 2027. "I'll be back fresh and ready to go for the business end of the season." Kane shared a quote from three-time Super Bowl-winning wide receiver Julian Edelman: "tough times don't last, tough people do", while thanking his supporters for their messages of support. Kane has a history of ankle issues although he has only missed a handful of games since moving to Bayern in 2023. England coach Thomas Tuchel will be keeping a keen eye out on how England's most capped player's rehabilitation progresses. England play Norway in the Nations League quarter-finals in late March. The injury comes at a difficult time for Bayern, who are currently missing several players, particularly up front. Bayern are without Luis Diaz, Serge Gnabry, Alphonso Davies, Ismael Saibari and captain Manuel Neuer, while midfielder Jamal Musiala and coach Vincent Kompany both returned after long lay-offs on Friday. dwi/pi

item.title: Premier League resumes, Kane facing spell on sidelines: football news – matchday live
item.description: ⚽️ All the latest match news and buildup for today’s games ⚽️ Today’s games | Tables | Kane injury news | And mail us An email has hit my inbox ‘re the lack of fancy Dan wingers', from Patrick Morgan: I don’t think you’re talking nonsense, but I’d say it’s tactical rather than a lack of talent. Look at Arsenal. Calafiori, Timber and White either bomb on or tuck into midfield, so the wide player has to work more like a No 8, working the half-space and tracking back, rather than being the classic ‘star man’ left high and wide to beat his full-back. Saka is the exception because he does both. A lot of Arsenal’s dynamism doesn’t come from out wide at all. It comes from Declan Rice driving through the middle like a very mobile siege engine. The 2015–2020 lot were mostly given licence to stay forward and decide games, and fewer managers allow that now. It works, but it can make Arsenal a bit stodgy to watch. That being said, I’d instantly forgive Sánchez and take him back over our other options. 60 goals in 120-odd league games, and he could knock out a number on the piano. Phwoar. Continue reading...

item.title: Giants news: Clean injury report, ‘baby DJ Reader,’ more
item.description: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to as the Giants look to bounce back as they host the Jacksonville Jaguars tomorrow. Giants’ schedule ramps up in difficulty with Sunday’s game against Jaguars | The Athletic The upcoming stretch of games will reveal whether the Giants are for real or just the beneficiaries of the easiest schedule in the league in the first 10 weeks of the season. The Giants’ first nine opponents have a combined .345 winning percentage. Their final eight opponents have a combined .566 winning percentage, which is the fourth highest in the league. The Jaguars defense will represent the toughest challenge for McCarthy. His first three starts were against the Houston Texans (18th in points allowed per game), the Philadelphia Eagles (19th) and the Washington Commanders (20th). The Jaguars are allowing 16 points per game, second best in the NFL. The Jaguars have been particularly stout against the run, allowing the sixth-fewest rushing yards per game. They rank in the top 10 in yards per carry allowed, rush defense expected points added and success rate on run plays. Boomer: Reese could be an all-time great Boomer says Arvell Reese can turn into one of the best linebackers in Giants history👀 pic.twitter.com/OT7rXVYDIl — WFAN Sports Radio (@WFAN660) November 19, 2026 Giants’ spark vs. Jaguars must be a return to West Virginia roots | New York Daily News The Giants can’t dwell on the opponent here, though. They need to stay focused on doing the basic elements correctly and consistently to be the best version of themselves. That’s the recipe. “It always is. That’s the formula,” tight end Chris Manhertz said. “I think it’s pretty simple from my vantage point: Take care of the ball, take care of your quarterback and execute at a high level. Assignment, technique have to be on point. Every man is handling their 1/11th. “Now it’s easier said than done,” he added. “There are people who are gonna win [their matchup] and people who are gonna lose. But I tend to believe if we’re able to do all of those things on a high level in three phases, the outcome is usually good. So the goal is always to put all three of those together in concert. And if there’s a void in one of those phases, the other two phases fill it and pick it up. But to me it’s simple.” NFL Week 11 preview: Picks, predictions, schedule | ESPN.com What we’re hearing on the Giants: The Giants don’t seem to like all the talk about facing the hard part of their schedule with Jacksonville, San Francisco, Seattle and Detroit looming over the next six weeks. The Jaguars are up first. The Giants aren’t panicking after a tough loss to the Commanders. “We’re so locked in right now on making sure that we worry about us,” offensive coordinator Matt Nagy said. New York is also out to prove it’s a good team. Stat to know: The Giants are averaging 6.2 yards per play with quarterback J.J. McCarthy on the field this season, compared to 4.7 with other quarterbacks. J.

McCarthy on the field this season, compared to 4.7 with other quarterbacks. J.J. McCarthy has the tools. Now Giants need him to deliver | The Record J.J. McCarthy was somewhat frazzled when he returned to the bench and sat down next to quarterbacks coach Brian Callahan seeking answers. Giants traded for McCarthy to be a stabilizer at QB if season went sideways. His job now with NFC East title in reach: win. Nothing else matters. “I’m not sitting there like a scout saying he can work on his plant foot or his follow-through.” Giants have been pushing the ball downfield 2026 aDOT Leaders 1. J.J. McCarthy (NYG) – 10.3 aDOT 2. C.J. Stroud (HOU) – 10.0 aDOT 3. Drake Maye (NE) – 9.8 aDOT pic.twitter.com/GFrNUMS6kV — Gridiron Stats and Info (@GridironInfo_) November 19, 2026 Every NFL Team’s Biggest Unanswered Question for the Second Half | Bleacher Report New York Giants: Is J.J. McCarthy a legit threat to Jaxson Dart? It’s early in his tenure with the team, but a fresh setting has seemingly brought out the best in McCarthy following a brutal run in Minnesota. What if he keeps rolling like this and leads the Giants to the playoffs? And what if, by chance, Dart returns for those playoffs? You’d have to stick with McCarthy, right? It could get awkward well before the offseason arrives. Sure-handed Malachi Fields becoming key piece in Giants ’ passing game | USAToday.com Likely no longer views Fields through a typical rookie lens. He described a player who understands the coverage picture and is prepared to win when the defense loads up against the primary options. “I don’t really look at Malachi as a rookie anymore. I look at him coming into his own player. So really just understand that if me and Leek are most likely getting most of the coverages, you’re going to have to win your one-on-ones,” Likely said. “And I feel like to this point, he’s been doing a great job of winning whenever he’s asked to win. And that’s most of the skill guys that get their opportunity. But Malachi’s definitely honed in on knowing that if I get one-on-one coverage, ball is most likely going to me. So I’ve just got to make my play.” The 10 best NFL player matchups to watch in Week 11 | PFF New York Giants WR Malik Nabers vs. Jacksonville Jaguars CB Travis Hunter. The Jaguars head to East Rutherford to meet the Giants in a clash between division leaders. Amid fun storylines in this one will be Nabers and Hunter going head-to-head. Nabers has looked all the way back from a devastating knee injury. His 76.0 PFF receiving grade slots 19th among qualified receivers, averaging 2.23 yards per route run. Hunter’s first season operating primarily as a cornerback has yielded strong results. His 77.4 PFF coverage grade is the sixth-highest among qualified corners, with his 8.5 snaps per target tied for 12th-best. Nabers has endured two tougher outings in his last two appearances, sitting at 1.30 yards per route run or lower in each. Given Hunter’s man-coverage proclivity, the receiver will need to be at his best against the athletic, physical second-year cover man. Giants player makes revealing admission about life before John Harbaugh: ‘It just hurt inside’ | NJ.com Earlier this week, Jermaine Eluemunor was chatting with John Harbaugh. Eluemunor, the Giants’ 10th-year right tackle, started thinking about how far this franchise had already come, halfway through Harbaugh’s first season. “In past years, I was already booking vacations for the offseason at this point in the year,” Eluemunor told Harbaugh. “Yes, you had eight games left, but we weren’t going anywhere,” said Eluemunor, reflecting on the Brian Daboll-era misery. “It wasn’t pointless and meaningless. But it just hurt inside knowing that we’re playing in games that don’t really matter. The type of team we had, everyone’s mindset was: The coach is getting fired.” From Big Blue View J.J. McCarthy has won at every level; will that continue in Giants’ playoff run? item.title: Horse Tracks: Does the AFC title go through Denver?
item.description: LAS VEGAS , NV - DECEMBER 7: Nik Bonitto (15) of the Denver Broncos celebrates sacking Geno Smith (7) of the Las Vegas Raiders during the third quarter of the Broncos' 24-17 win at Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas, Nevada on Sunday, December 7, 2025. (Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images Good morning, Broncos Country! Several AFC teams swiftly moved up in the conference rankings last weekend while the Broncos quietly dropped to fifth overall, making their path to and through the postseason a little more challenging. But that means nothing to Broncos Country. While the rest of the country was seeing cracks in the Orange and Blue, this fanbase saw more opportunity to flex some muscle in the remaining weeks. And prove some (many) people wrong. While a lot of people believe the road to the Super Bowl will go through the Bills, if not the Bengals, not too many outside of Colorado believe it will go through Denver. Which is kinda awesome, because I’ve always preferred it when Denver plays the role of the underdogs ( versus the overdogs — sorry Bo! ) to the media hype. But man, if Broncos Country just won’t give up on this team! A whopping 64% of fans believe it will be Denver who wins the AFC, which is 46% percent more than the crew picking the Bills (18%) or the number giving the honor to the Bengals (11%). Perhaps my favorite number in the whole survey — even more than the large majority picking the Broncos — is the very small 2% who believe the AFC title will belong to the Chiefs by season’s end. Hahahahahahahahahahahahaha. Either way, nothing happens without winning most if not all of the remaining games, and that starts by taking care of business this weekend at Mile High against the hated Raiduhs .

Perhaps my favorite number in the whole survey — even more than the large majority picking the Broncos — is the very small 2% who believe the AFC title will belong to the Chiefs by season’s end. Hahahahahahahahahahahahaha. Either way, nothing happens without winning most if not all of the remaining games, and that starts by taking care of business this weekend at Mile High against the hated Raiduhs .

item.title: Brad Gilbert has a theory for why Carlos Alcaraz is getting injured so much, ‘not everyone can be like Federer’
item.description: Carlos Alcaraz has endured an injury-riddled year, which has seen him miss more than four months of competitive action. His absence from the ATP Tour left a massive vacuum, with Alexander Zverev the generous beneficiary to his faltering fitness. Despite the hardships endured after spending so long on the sidelines, many did predict that the Spaniard could use this rest time to return reinvigorated at the end of the season . Winning titles in Tokyo, Vienna and Paris has certainly proven that suggestion correct. However, the ATP Finals is the one he will really be keen to capture, and based on his matches so far, it feels hard to bet against him. That being said, it must be noted that Alcaraz has picked up a hamstring injury during his comfortable group-stage run, with Brad Gilbert looking ahead to how this might shape the tournament. Why does Carlos Alcaraz get injured so often? Speaking on the Big T podcast , after he had previewed Carlos Alcaraz ’s upcoming semi-final vs Ben Shelton, the American pundit and coach was asked why he thinks the 23-year-old suffers so often from injury. After all, whilst this year’s wrist issue has been the worst of his career to date, he has endured plenty of health concerns over the years; certainly enough to raise alarm bells. Comparing Alcaraz to Rafael Nadal, whose super-physical play style saw his body break down time and time again, Gilbert insisted: “Well, I mean, injuries are part of every sport. They’re part of tennis. Not everybody can be like Fed and just play elegantly. And actually, Djokovic had an incredibly long run of being pretty healthy as well. “So some players are a little unluckier; some game styles are a little more physical. I do think that Alcaraz’s style is physical, like Rafa. It’s a little bit physically demanding. “Fans want to see the dynamics. They want to see Carlos doing these incredible things out there; sometimes it can be a little bit taxing on the body when you’re running five corners, and then you hit some outrageous shot. I love seeing it myself. But unfortunately, I go back to the, you know, availability is the best availability, and his style, at 23, what do you think it’ll be like when he’s 28? “He’s gonna have some. Same with Rafa, but he managed it for 20 years.” Brad Gilbert previews Carlos Alcaraz’s ATP Finals match vs Ben Shelton Gilbert’s analysis of today’s standout ATP Finals showdown was unsurprisingly dominated by Juan Carlos Ferrero. item.content:encoded: Carlos Alcaraz has endured an injury-riddled year, which has seen him miss more than four months of competitive action. Despite the hardships endured after spending so long on the sidelines, many did predict that the Spaniard could use this rest time to return reinvigorated at the end of the season . And actually, Djokovic had an incredibly long run of being pretty healthy as well. “So some players are a little unluckier; some game styles are a little more physical. I do think that Alcaraz’s style is physical, like Rafa. It’s a little bit physically demanding. “Fans want to see the dynamics. They want to see Carlos doing these incredible things out there; sometimes it can be a little bit taxing on the body when you’re running five corners, and then you hit some outrageous shot. I love seeing it myself. But unfortunately, I go back to the, you know, availability is the best availability, and his style, at 23, what do you think it’ll be like when he’s 28? “He’s gonna have some. Same with Rafa, but he managed it for 20 years.” Brad Gilbert previews Carlos Alcaraz’s ATP Finals match vs Ben Shelton Gilbert’s analysis of today’s standout ATP Finals showdown was unsurprisingly dominated by Juan Carlos Ferrero. After all, whilst he did help Shelton during his Paris Masters final defeat to Alcaraz, he was not present in his box. Today, he will be. Gilbert, who actually spoke to Ferrero not long ago, had some advice for the Spanish coach ahead of his first official match against his former pupil. Photo by Dimitar DILKOFF / AFP via Getty Images He suggested: “I think he needs to be a lot more aggressive off the first ball and try to win more points off of the first or second ball, because as the rally kind of gets lengthened, or if Alcaraz gets a ball from neutral, that’s where the pendulum really swings for Carlos. “I think he needs to be a lot more aggressive, and I also like to see him serve way more aggressively. Try to win points off that first serve, you know, ’cause I think that’s more frustrating when you play a big server, and you’re not getting into rallies.” Due to his injury, Alcaraz went big against Flavio Cobolli and reaped the benefits of a quick and easy match. Discussing whether now playing Shelton, who historically likes to keep the points short anyway, will benefit the seven-time major champion, Gilbert added: “I’ve heard you guys talk about, you know, here in Paris, how quick these courts are. And yet I’m seeing a lot of rallies. Actually, Ben does like to get in rallies. “So maybe if you are JCF and Ben and Bryan, you’re thinking about, okay, what you watched today was the guy playing at Mach 10 speed. Maybe we want to try to extend some rallies to see how his movement is. “He had the legs strapped up. He’s got the knees. So he’s a little bit banged up, played a lot of tennis in the last, you know, five, six weeks, after not playing any tennis, and he’s supposedly supposed to play Davis Cup next week.” Gilbert finished by reiterating that, whilst Shelton and Ferrero will want to win this match, his pre-season ahead of the Australian Open is what really matters for their new professional relationship.

item.title: Women’s Sports Have Gotten Too Big for Small Stadiums
item.description: Women’s sports are bigger than ever. And yet, several championship-contending women’s basketball and soccer teams found themselves in scheduling conundrums this fall. During last month’s WNBA Finals, the league rescheduled three games so the Atlanta Dream could move their home games from the 3,500-seat Gateway Center Arena to the Hawks’ 17,000-person State Farm Arena. Since the Dream don’t normally play in State Farm, the venue had not been blocked out for the WNBA Finals during the league’s original dates, resulting in a highly criticized Thursday afternoon Game 6 . In the NWSL, the three highest-seeded teams in the playoffs all faced conflicts at their home venues, which they do not own, during the semifinals weekend. The Washington Spirit ended up playing their semifinal last Saturday with college football lines painted on the field . The team hosting the Sunday semifinal, Gotham FC, moved the match to a smaller venue due to poor pitch conditions at their “overscheduled” home stadium , which is owned by MLS team New York Red Bulls. “This league deserves better,” Gotham coach Juan Carlos Amorós said after his team lost 2–1 to the Kansas City Current. “The two arguably best teams, most consistent, having to deal with these situations.” John Jones-Imagn Images It’s not just a problem for women’s sports: MLS’s Chicago Fire, for example, can’t host their playoff game at Soldier Field on Sunday due to a Chicago Bears game. But the recent string of scheduling scrambles highlights some of the growing pains that come with the rapid rise of women’s sports, and raises questions about how women’s teams can prevent these kinds of issues in the future. NWSL commissioner Jessica Berman said it’s “clear we have more work to do” on infrastructure in her end-of-season press conference Thursday in Washington, D.C. Berman said the league needs to prioritize venues it can control or influence, whether through teams owning their stadiums, sharing venue ownership with MLS teams, or having strategic partnerships that prioritize an NWSL team that is a tenant. In recent expansion processes, the WNBA and NWSL have both chosen ownership groups that already own a men’s team or, in the NWSL’s case, are building their own stadium. The team that beat the Dream in the WNBA Finals , the Golden State Valkyries, proved why a shared ownership set-up can solve scheduling headaches. The Valkyries, who have the same owners as the NBA’s Warriors and the Chase Center, were set to host Game 2 of the WNBA Finals in San Francisco on the same date as a Doja Cat concert at the arena. Contingency dates are standard practice across NBA arenas. item.content:encoded: Women’s sports are bigger than ever. And yet, several championship-contending women’s basketball and soccer teams found themselves in scheduling conundrums this fall. During last month’s WNBA Finals, the league rescheduled three games so the Atlanta Dream could move their home games from the 3,500-seat Gateway Center Arena to the Hawks’ 17,000-person State Farm Arena. Since the Dream don’t normally play in State Farm, the venue had not been blocked out for the WNBA Finals during the league’s original dates, resulting in a highly criticized Thursday afternoon Game 6 . In the NWSL, the three highest-seeded teams in the playoffs all faced conflicts at their home venues, which they do not own, during the semifinals weekend. The Washington Spirit ended up playing their semifinal last Saturday with college football lines painted on the field . The team hosting the Sunday semifinal, Gotham FC, moved the match to a smaller venue due to poor pitch conditions at their “overscheduled” home stadium , which is owned by MLS team New York Red Bulls. “This league deserves better,” Gotham coach Juan Carlos Amorós said after his team lost 2–1 to the Kansas City Current. “The two arguably best teams, most consistent, having to deal with these situations.” John Jones-Imagn Images It’s not just a problem for women’s sports: MLS’s Chicago Fire, for example, can’t host their playoff game at Soldier Field on Sunday due to a Chicago Bears game. But the recent string of scheduling scrambles highlights some of the growing pains that come with the rapid rise of women’s sports, and raises questions about how women’s teams can prevent these kinds of issues in the future. NWSL commissioner Jessica Berman said it’s “clear we have more work to do” on infrastructure in her end-of-season press conference Thursday in Washington, D.C. Berman said the league needs to prioritize venues it can control or influence, whether through teams owning their stadiums, sharing venue ownership with MLS teams, or having strategic partnerships that prioritize an NWSL team that is a tenant. In recent expansion processes, the WNBA and NWSL have both chosen ownership groups that already own a men’s team or, in the NWSL’s case, are building their own stadium. The team that beat the Dream in the WNBA Finals , the Golden State Valkyries, proved why a shared ownership set-up can solve scheduling headaches. The Valkyries, who have the same owners as the NBA’s Warriors and the Chase Center, were set to host Game 2 of the WNBA Finals in San Francisco on the same date as a Doja Cat concert at the arena. Once the Valkyries advanced to the Finals, the concert was moved. A Valkyries representative said it was “standard practice” to have contingency dates for postseason games. Contingency dates are standard practice across NBA arenas. Jerry Goldman, a vice president for booking at the Chicago Bulls’ and Blackhawks’ United Center, told Front Office Sports the United Center ensures that contracts for events such as concerts and private events scheduled from April to June—normally the NBA and NHL playoffs window—include backup dates. “When you book during the playoffs, they know,” Goldman said. “We put it in their agreement like, ‘Your contingency date is this.’ Everybody knows.” The Washington Spirit are going to incorporate contingency dates going forward, the team’s CEO Kim Stone told FOS on Thursday at NWSL media day. The Spirit’s Audi Field is operated by D.C. United, and a spokesperson for the MLS team told FOS that the stadium booked Nov. 14’s Division III Secretaries Cup between the Merchant Marine Academy and Coast Guard Academy in spring of 2025. “Both partners wanted to be at Audi, and we found a way to make it work,” D.C. United’s president of business operations Danita Johnson, told FOS last week. Stone, who managed arenas for the NBA’s Heat and Warriors before joining the Spirit, credited Johnson for making the NWSL semifinal and Secretaries Cup double-header at Audi Field a reality. And, she said, the two teams are going to try to avoid that drama in the future. “We’re going to apply the lessons learned on a go-forward basis, and it’s really simple, [Johnson will] book a contingency date on any events that are scheduled for a playoff game,” Stone said. “As long as everybody’s committed to it, we won’t have that again.” Growing Pains In the WNBA, scheduling issues are nothing new, but they used to receive significantly less attention. The Dream, who were a State Farm Arena tenant until 2019, were forced to move Game 3 of the 2013 WNBA Finals, their last Finals appearance, to the 13,000-seat Gas South Arena about 25 miles away from downtown Atlanta due a conflict with Disney On Ice . Only about 5,000 fans came to that game. But in 2024, the draft class led by Caitlin Clark and current Dream player Angel Reese brought new attention to the league. WNBA games consistently started selling out NBA arenas, and teams that played in smaller venues started moving some home games to accommodate larger audiences. The Dream felt the increased demand, selling out every single home game at Gateway Center since 2024. In response, team president Morgan Shaw Parker told FOS ahead of the 2025 season that they were actively looking for ways to move into a bigger venue. Then ahead of the Finals, the team announced it had agreed to a deal with State Farm to play all of its games at the NBA venue starting next season. Brett Davis-Imagn Images Had the Dream, who quickly turned into a championship contender after trading for Reese in April , been a yearlong tenant at State Farm this season, the WNBA Finals dates likely would’ve been accounted for. State Farm CEO Steve Koonin told FOS that they plan to hold playoff dates for the Dream through the duration of their five-year deal. Many WNBA fans were clamoring for the Hawks to move regular-season games that coincided with Games 4 and 6 of the WNBA Finals. The team did adjust start times, but did not move the dates. A Sombr concert that conflicted with Game 3 in Atlanta went ahead as scheduled, and the WNBA instead changed its date. One of the reasons the WNBA could move the three games in Atlanta was because of its media partner, first-time Finals broadcaster USA Network. The network approved each rescheduling, even a less-than-ideal TV window of 12:30 p.m. ET on a Thursday. That level of flexibility is unusual in a sports media landscape constantly striving for viewership records and higher ad revenue. The NWSL, for example, worked around its seminal broadcast windows of Saturday afternoon on CBS and Sunday afternoon on ABC. Dream owner Renee Montgomery described the Finals rescheduling to FOS as a “ group project ” involving both teams, the leagues (NBA and WNBA), and broadcast partners. USA Network declined to comment on this story. ‘Something Has To Change’ In sports, venue scheduling happens months, sometimes years, ahead of time. An NFL spokesperson told FOS the league generally gives teams playoff dates about a year and a half to two years out. An MLB spokesperson told FOS teams know about a year and a half out when the postseason will start and when the World Series will be. An NBA spokesperson told FOS the league gives teams playoff dates the summer before they happen, roughly nine months out. An NHL spokesperson did not respond to questions. The United Center’s Goldman said he typically works with the Bulls and Blackhawks a year in advance to plan their schedules. The WNBA and NWSL each gave lead time to try to avoid any problems, but still ended up with scheduling headaches this fall. The WNBA gave its teams playoff hold dates for home venues in December 2025, a source confirmed to FOS . Dream owners said in an open letter late last month they warned the league two months earlier about the possible Finals venue conflict with State Farm. The NWSL publicly posted its 2026 playoff dates in July 2025, but by that point, Audi Field had already

item.title: Lamar Jackson’s camp hits back at critics blaming him for Ravens’ struggles
item.description: Lamar Jackson ’s camp has pushed back against criticism surrounding the NFL quarterback’s injury history and availability during the Baltimore Ravens ’ disappointing season. Lamar Jackson Entertainment shared a pointed message on X Saturday, questioning whether Jackson should carry the blame for Baltimore’s problems. “So, is it Lamar’s fault again? Or are Lamar’s injuries still an unsolved mystery?” the account posted. MORE: NFL analyst rips Marlon Humphrey over controversial Baltimore remarks The message accompanied a video compilation showing the hits Jackson and other Baltimore quarterbacks have taken this season. It also highlighted poor pass protection and questioned whether the offensive line deserves greater scrutiny. So, is it Lamar’s fault again? Or are Lamar’s injuries still an unsolved mystery? 🤔🙄 pic.twitter.com/aLyV0rHlHs — Lamar Jackson Entertainment 💽 (@lamarjacksonent) November 21, 2026 The post comes after Jackson suffered a broken and dislocated right thumb against the Buffalo Bills on November 1. He sustained the injury on his first offensive snap after returning from a high ankle sprain. Jackson underwent surgery and landed on injured reserve. His recovery timeline is estimated at six to ten weeks. The quarterback had already missed three games with the ankle injury. His limited availability has fueled criticism as Baltimore struggles through a five-game losing streak. Lamar Jackson’s camp points toward wider problems in Baltimore Atlanta, Georgia, USA; Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson (8) during the second quarter against the Atlanta Falcons at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) The compilation also featured injuries suffered by Baltimore’s other quarterbacks. One clip showed Tyler Huntley’s turf toe, which was a season-ending injury, and another showed Jacoby Brissett taking a hard hit against the Los Angeles Chargers. The message questioned whether those injuries should also be blamed on Jackson. It effectively shifted attention toward the team’s pass protection rather than the quarterback’s durability. The video also addressed claims that Jackson falls asleep during team meetings. It included pictures showing him sitting in the front row as proof against the rumors. Jackson has appeared in only five games this season, completing 70.1% of his passes for 967 yards and six touchdowns. Baltimore has used multiple quarterbacks during his absence and now sits at 4-6. MORE: Ravens WAG apologizes for calling Baltimore ‘scary’ amid Marlon Humphrey fiasco The Ravens’ offensive struggles extend beyond their quarterback situation. The team ranks 22nd in scoring and has struggled to maintain consistency. Jackson’s camp clearly wants critics to consider the circumstances behind his injuries. However, Baltimore must find answers fast as its season continues slipping away. — Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trending stories with The Big Lead N

item.title: Blue Jays Fans Get Unfortunate Kevin Gausman Reunion Update
item.description: TORONTO, ONTARIO - OCTOBER 31: Kevin Gausman #34 of the Toronto Blue Jays looks on against the Los Angeles Dodgers during the first inning in game six of the 2025 World Series at Rogers Center on October 31, 2025 in Toronto, Ontario. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) Getty Images Toronto Blue Jays fans have plenty to keep an eye on as the organization navigates an important offseason following a disappointing season. General manager Ross Atkins and the front office are already making roster adjustments, most recently claiming shortstop Christian Cairo off waivers from the Los Angeles Dodgers and designating reliever Chase Lee for assignment. The Blue Jays are also exploring ways to strengthen their pitching staff, with free-agent possibilities such as Tarik Skubal and Freddy Peralta drawing attention as the club considers its options for 2027. But Toronto’s offseason has also brought renewed attention to a former member of its rotation whose future remains uncertain. Kevin Gausman reached free agency shortly after being traded to the Chicago Cubs. Now, as many fans remain hopeful for a reunion that would bring Gausman back, news has surfaced that he has formally closed a personal chapter in Toronto. “Gausman, who played four-and-a-half seasons with the Jays before being dealt to the Chicago Cubs at this year’s trade deadline, appears to have sold his Lawrence Park mansion after almost a month on the market,” Dan Bilicki r eported for the Toronto Sun . FORBES | By Peter Chawaga Yankees Trade Bust Frankie Montas Gets Surprise Return Update Kevin Gausman Home Sale Casts Doubt On Toronto Blue Jays Reunion The property sale is a disappointing update for fans who might have been hoping that Gausman’s long ties to Toronto would have made a Blue Jays reunion quick and easy. Although the 35-year-old has not publicly committed to continuing his playing career, a return to the Blue Jays remains a possibility worth monitoring as free agency unfolds, though he’d now have to find a new place to live if he returns. “Since the sale is still conditional, it’s unknown how much the gorgeous property officially sold for, though it’s all but certain that the Gausmans took a loss on the transaction,” Bilicki added. FORBES | By Peter Chawaga Red Sox Finally Close Ugly Mookie Betts Chapter WIth Unceremonious Cut Toronto Blue Jays Fan Favorite Kevin Gausman Remains Available For Return Even after the home sale, the Blue Jays could be considering a return for Gausman. “After talking about potential retirement in spring this year, Gausman is probably looking at a one-year deal,” The Athletic’s Mitch Bannon reported . “But what if another team comes with a juicy multiyear offer? Gausman was open to an extension with the Jays ahead of the deadline last year, but the sides never got the ball rolling. With other teams likely to be interested this offseason, will the Jays and Gausman be able to line up on money now?” Gausman originally joined Toronto on a five-year, $110 mil
