item.title: Arsenal loses another player to injury
item.description: Arsenal loses another player to injury Martin Zubimendi has suffered another injury just when it appeared he was about to get more opportunities to play for Arsenal. The midfielder has struggled to maintain his fitness and secure a regular place in the Gunners’ starting line-up, making the latest setback an unwanted development. Zubimendi was one of the first names on the team sheet last season, but his involvement has been reduced during the current campaign. Although Arsenal continue to regard him as an important member of the squad, he has lost his place in the starting eleven and is working to regain his position. The Spaniard impressed while representing Spain during the international break and was expected to feature against Newcastle United . However, his hopes of getting minutes in the fixture have been disrupted after suffering another fitness problem. Arteta confirms fresh injury setback Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta has confirmed that Zubimendi will miss the upcoming matches after medical examinations revealed a hamstring injury. The midfielder initially returned from international duty believing he was in good condition and was not particularly concerned about the problem. However, further assessment revealed an injury that will keep him out of action for several weeks. The development is disappointing for both the player and Arsenal, especially as he was hoping to use the coming fixtures to strengthen his claim for a regular starting position. (Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images) Zubimendi faces spell on the sidelines Speaking via Arsenal Media , Arteta provided an update on the midfielder’s condition and confirmed that he would be unavailable for selection. “He’s out; unfortunately, he has a slight problem in his hamstring. “He wasn’t too concerned to be fair after the game, but after the MRI scans, it showed that there is an injury there and he’s going to be out for a few weeks.” For Arsenal, losing the Spaniard is an unwanted setback as they continue their campaign. Meanwhile, Zubimendi will be hoping to recover quickly and return in good condition so he can compete for his place in Arteta’s midfield. His immediate priority will be completing his recovery before attempting to establish himself as a regular starter again. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ ADMIN COMMENT So here are some simple rules which I must insist commenters follow…. Arteta confirms fresh injury setback Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta has confirmed that Zubimendi will miss the upcoming matches after medical examinations revealed a hamstring injury. The midfielder initially returned from international duty believing he was in good condition and was not particularly concerned about the problem. However, further assessment revealed an injury that will keep him out of action for several weeks. The development is disappointing for both the player and Arsenal, especially as he was hoping to use the coming fixtures to strengthen his claim for a regular starting position. (Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images) Zubimendi faces spell on the sidelines Speaking via Arsenal Media , Arteta provided an update on the midfielder’s condition and confirmed that he would be unavailable for selection. “He’s out; unfortunately, he has a slight problem in his hamstring. “He wasn’t too concerned to be fair after the game, but after the MRI scans, it showed that there is an injury there and he’s going to be out for a few weeks.” For Arsenal, losing the Spaniard is an unwanted setback as they continue their campaign. Meanwhile, Zubimendi will be hoping to recover quickly and return in good condition so he can compete for his place in Arteta’s midfield. His immediate priority will be completing his recovery before attempting to establish himself as a regular starter again. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ ADMIN COMMENT So here are some simple rules which I must insist commenters follow…. item.title: Twitter Gold: Introducing The Stupid Chronicles
item.description: LEXINGTON, KY - NOVEMBER 16: Grambling Tigers guard Dwayne Pierce (11) in a game between the Grambling State Tigers and the Kentucky Wildcats on November 16, 2026, at Rupp Arena in Lexington, KY. (Photo by Jeff Moreland/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Have you seen what happened in the Grambling State-Southern Mississippi game? This really is in the category of it has to be seen to be believed. Grambling was up 87-83 with less than a second on the clock in overtime, and still lost . Here’s what happened: Southern Mississippi’s Elliot Tulip tried a three-pointer with time running down with 0:00.9 on the clock, and was fouled. He went to the line and nailed the first two shots, but the third one bounced off the backboard. A teammate tried to tip it in, but it didn’t hit the rim, so the ball was dead. All Grambling had to do was to get the ball inbounds. Even with a steal, as long as it wasn’t under the basket, there wasn’t enough time for Southern Miss to get a shot off. Only Grambling’s Hassan Washington felt that Chandler Watts was too close to him, so he ddi the only logical thing: he threw him to the ground, drawing a flagrant foul. Just kidding. What an idiotic thing to do with the game on the line. Watts went to the line and hit both. Southern Miss got the ball in and Tulip got a shot off, but it missed. Can you imagine if he’d hit it? He would have scored 5 points in less than a second and won the game. Odds are no one has ever done that, and the chances of it happening again would be pretty slim, too. Southern Miss ultimately won in double OT. Never seen anything like it. We have video!! Here is how to Give up 5 Free Throws, Possession and blow a 4-point lead in 0 Seconds (Grambling vs Southern Miss) https://t.co/PSasX78zRe pic.twitter.com/0nch4xisdB — NCAA Buzzer Beaters & Game Winners (@NCAABuzzerBters) November 21, 2026

item.title: Fans don’t expect Michigan to cover vs UCLA
item.description: Michigan head coach Kyle Whittingham talks to a referee regarding a play against Oklahoma during the first half at Michigan Stadium in Ann Arbor on Saturday, Sept. 12, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Earlier this week, we asked fans if they believe Michigan will cover the spread against UCLA. Now, the results are in. Just 17% of voters believe Michigan will cover the spread. Per FanDuel Sportsbook , Michigan is a 3.5-point underdog. The spread is surprising — while many perceive UCLA’s schedule as ‘weak’, they’re still 10-0, and Michigan is just 5-5. UCLA has beaten teams that Michigan has not, including Oregon, Michigan State, and Minnesota — what does that say about Michigan? Further, home-field advantage is dicey this week. Tickets are hovering around $14 online right now, with thousands still for sale. The weather won’t be advantageous either — UCLA will experience warm November weather in Ann Arbor, with the game temperature being sunny and between 60 and 65 degrees. Michigan receiver JJ Buchanan will be out, head coach Kyle Whittingham is on the hot seat, and interim offensive coordinator Jim Harding hasn’t been inspiring — there are too many variables that seem to be working against Michigan covering the spread.

item.title: Is there a striker you think Bayern Munich can get in January?
item.description: (Photo by Lukasz Germaniuk/Eurasia Sport Images/Getty Images) | Getty Images Bayern Munich could be heading toward an unexpectedly busy January transfer window, and the club might not have much choice but to explore the striker m arket. Harry Kane reportedly suffered a syndesmosis tear that could keep him sidelined for as long as three mont hs. Losing the England international for that length of time would be a massive blow, particularly with Bayern competing on multiple fronts and needing a reliable goal-scoring presence. Unfortunately, Kane is not the only attacking concern. Saibari is facing an extended absenc e of his own after undergoing surgery for a syndesmotic ligament injury in his right ankle, while Serge Gnabry is expected to miss the remainder of the year with a hamstring injury. That leaves Vincent Kompany with considerably fewer attacking options and puts additional pressure on the players who remain availab le. Bayern had previously been expected to avoid January business, preferring to preserve its resources for a major attacking signing next summer. However, the injury situation could force Max Eberl and Christoph Freund to reconsider that approach. A short-term loan might make the most sense. Who could Bayern Munich realistically target in January to help fill the void? Is there a striker you would like to see the c lub pu rsue? Join the conversation! item.title: European-Japanese BepiColombo probe arrives in orbit around Mercury today
item.description: null Mercury is about to receive a robotic visitor from Earth. The BepiColombo mission — a joint effort of the European Space Agency (ESA) and the Japanese Aerospace Exploration Agency ( JAXA ) — will arrive in orbit around Mercury today (Nov. 21), more than eight years after leaving its home planet. The big moment will come after an orbit-insertion burn, which is scheduled to begin today at 1:24 p.m. EST (1824 GMT) and last for 37 minutes. BepiColombo consists of two main spacecraft: ESA's Mercury Planetary Orbiter (MPO) and JAXA's Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter (MMO), also known as Mio. The duo launched — along with a power and propulsion element called the Mercury Transfer Module (MTM) — aboard an Ariane 5 rocket from French Guiana in October 2018 , beginning a long and looping trip through the inner solar system. Mercury is a difficult planet to reach because it's so close to the sun . Spacecraft approaching the solar system's innermost planet are accelerated to high velocities by the immense gravitational pull of our star and must shed a great deal of kinetic energy to be captured by Mercury's much weaker tug. So the BepiColombo team designed a trajectory that featured one flyby of Earth , two of Venus and six of Mercury over the course of about seven years. That flight time was increased by a year , however, after the mission suffered an issue with its solar panels, which reduced the power available for the MTM's electric thrusters. BepiColombo's arrival at Mercury will take a total of about six months. (Image credit: European Space Agency) Today's orbital insertion is the latest milestone in BepiColombo's Mercury arrival phase, which is expected to take about six months in total. Arrival began on Sept. 3, when the MTM released MPO and Mio. The two orbiters remain connected today; they won't separate until Dec. 9 or thereabouts. Shortly thereafter, Mio will settle into its final orbit, a highly elliptical path that will take it over Mercury's poles. MPO is also destined for a polar orbit, though a much less elliptical one than Mio's; the ESA probe will conduct a series of engine burns before finally getting there on March 10, 2027. BepiColombo won't start doing science work until April 6, 2027. The two probes will gather complementary data from their two different vantage points, shedding a great deal of light on a mysterious world. "The mission will study all aspects of Mercury, from the structure and dynamics of its magnetosphere and how it interacts with the solar wind , to its internal structure with its large iron core, and the origin of the planet’s magnetic field," ESA officials wrote in a BepiColombo mission description . "The data will enable scientists to understand more about the origin and evolution of a planet located close to its parent star, and a better understanding of the overall evolution of our solar system," they added.

item.title: 'Accept cookies'? Russia collects data from swaths of unknowing Swedes
item.description: A Russian tech firm backed by an oligarch close to President Vladimir Putin has secretly been collecting data from hundreds of thousands – possibly millions – of Swedes, a newspaper investigation found. The revelation has rattled the Nordic nation, whose proximity to Russia and unusually open public records system make it particularly vulnerable to Moscow’s hybrid war tactics.

item.title: 2027: We’re not joining your opposition coalition, PDP tells Lukman
item.description: …Snubs November 30 summit, declares Wike’s Rainbow alliance its only coalition By Luminous Jannamike, Abuja The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) has rejected claims that it has joined the opposition Coalition for Democracy being promoted by former National Vice Chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Salihu Lukman, declaring that it will not attend the coalition’s November 30 summit. The party said it had not entered into any alliance with the coalition, authorised anyone to represent it at the summit or agreed to be bound by any decision taken in its name. It maintained that its only recognised coalition arrangement was the Rainbow Coalition, backed by its National Leader, Nyesom Wike. The position was contained in a statement signed by the PDP National Publicity Secretary, Hon. Jungudo Haruna Mohammed, who said those being presented as the party’s representatives were expelled members with no authority to speak or act on its behalf. Jungudo said the individuals’ claims to the party’s leadership and representation had suffered defeats at the Federal High Court, Court of Appeal and Supreme Court. He added that the courts had issued orders restraining Kabiru Tanimu Turaki, SAN, and his associates from parading themselves as PDP leaders, while imposing financial penalties exceeding N100 million over alleged abuses of court processes and frivolous litigation. Questioning Lukman’s continued engagement with the individuals, Jungudo said, “It is therefore astonishing that Mr Salihu Lukman, who ought to be sufficiently informed about the legal status and recognised leadership of the PDP, would continue to engage these individuals and use them as a basis for associating the party with his so-called Toronto Coalition.” Describing the proposed arrangement as a political project built on misrepresentation, the PDP declared it ‘dead on arrival’, particularly because those being presented as its representatives lacked the authority to speak on its behalf. The party also threatened legal action against Lukman, his associates and other promoters of the Coalition for Democracy if they continued to use its name and institutional identity in their political activities. “The party will not hesitate to pursue appropriate legal action against any person or group that continues to unlawfully associate the PDP with this arrangement,” Jungudo warned. Reiterating its position, the party said the Rainbow Coalition, in line with Wike’s political direction and directives, remained its only recognised coalition arrangement. It consequently urged Nigerians, political stakeholders, members and supporters, as well as media organisations, to disregard reports linking its national headquarters at Wadata Plaza, Abuja, to the November 30 summit or any other political arrangement being promoted by Lukman and his associates. “The PDP will not allow its identity to be hijacked, its institutional authority misrepresented or its political interests compromised by individuals who

item.title: The Governor, The Candidate And The Voter
item.description: Anambra puts the power of endorsements to the test, while opposition negotiations and election safeguards face approaching deadlines. In Awka, the message was partnership with the centre. In Onitsha, Obi demonstrated his continuing ability to mobilise in the state he once governed. The electoral question lies between those pictures: how far can a governor’s endorsement move presidential votes, and how effectively can a candidate convert personal loyalty into turnout? Anambra will help answer both. Soludo’s Wager APGA’s support gives Tinubu an organised partner outside the APC. Soludo is making an argument about the South-East’s place in national politics: that cooperation with the President offers a route to influence and development. The presentation reaffirmed APGA’s presidential alignment while the party continues pursuing its own interests in other elections. For Tinubu, the opportunity lies in improving his reach through a political organisation rooted in the state. For Soludo, the challenge is to persuade people who support his governorship to make the same choice in a presidential contest. Those loyalties need not coincide. Voters can approve of a governor’s performance and prefer another presidential candidate. They can also reconsider a previous choice if a new alliance offers a convincing case. The evidence will emerge through sustained mobilisation, local organisation and ultimately the ballot. A flag presentation establishes an endorsement. It cannot establish the electorate’s response. Obi’s Home-State Test Obi’s Onitsha road show supplies evidence of campaign activity and visible support. It does not, on its own, measure the balance of opinion across Anambra. His task is to maintain that support while building sufficient reach elsewhere. The home-state contest also brings his governing record into sharper focus. Obi has chosen to defend that record publicly; Soludo is advancing a different argument about Anambra’s political interests. Voters deserve an exchange grounded in verifiable achievements, present needs and credible proposals. It offers a clear case study in the relationship between party machinery, a governor’s influence and a candidate’s personal following. item.content:encoded: Anambra puts the power of endorsements to the test, while opposition negotiations and election safeguards face approaching deadlines. On Thursday in Awka, Governor Chukwuma Soludo presented APGA’s flag to Vice-President Kashim Shettima, who received it on behalf of President Bola Tinubu. On Friday, Peter Obi took his campaign through Onitsha, attracting supporters ahead of his town hall engagement. Two neighbouring cities offered competing pictures of political strength. In Awka, the message was partnership with the centre. In Onitsha, Obi demonstrated his continuing ability to mobilise in the state he once governed. The electoral question lies between those pictures: how far can a governor’s endorsement move presidential votes, and how effectively can a candidate convert personal loyalty into turnout? Anambra will help answer both. Soludo’s Wager APGA’s support gives Tinubu an organised partner outside the APC. Soludo is making an argument about the South-East’s place in national politics: that cooperation with the President offers a route to influence and development. The presentation reaffirmed APGA’s presidential alignment while the party continues pursuing its own interests in other elections. For Tinubu, the opportunity lies in improving his reach through a political organisation rooted in the state. For Soludo, the challenge is to persuade people who support his governorship to make the same choice in a presidential contest. Those loyalties need not coincide. Voters can approve of a governor’s performance and prefer another presidential candidate. They can also reconsider a previous choice if a new alliance offers a convincing case. The evidence will emerge through sustained mobilisation, local organisation and ultimately the ballot. A flag presentation establishes an endorsement. It cannot establish the electorate’s response. Obi’s Home-State Test Obi’s Onitsha road show supplies evidence of campaign activity and visible support. It does not, on its own, measure the balance of opinion across Anambra. His task is to maintain that support while building sufficient reach elsewhere. The home-state contest also brings his governing record into sharper focus. Obi has chosen to defend that record publicly; Soludo is advancing a different argument about Anambra’s political interests. Voters deserve an exchange grounded in verifiable achievements, present needs and credible proposals. Claims that cooperation necessarily delivers prosperity or that popular enthusiasm guarantees victory require testing. Anambra’s significance extends beyond its presidential tally. It offers a clear case study in the relationship between party machinery, a governor’s influence and a candidate’s personal following. Opposition Unity Loses Another Week The Coalition for Democracy has postponed its second summit from November 23 to November 30, citing member parties’ campaign schedules. The organisers say participating parties have agreed to suspend campaign activities on the new date so their leaders can attend. The explanation is plausible. Presidential candidates have demanding itineraries. The political cost is time. Every week spent negotiating leaves less time to explain an agreement, reconcile local interests and organise around it. The postponement also illustrates the coalition’s central difficulty: its members are campaigning separately while trying to determine how they should cooperate. That does not make the undertaking futile. Cooperation on electoral integrity, campaign freedoms and policy priorities could have value even without one presidential ticket. But the summit’s eventual significance will depend on the obligations it creates. Who signs? Who is authorised to commit each party? What work begins immediately afterward? For the ADC, NDC, APM, SDP, PRP and participating PDP representatives, attendance will be the first test. Implementation will be the more demanding one. ADC: A Clearer INEC Position, an Unresolved Appeal Fresh reporting provides an important update on INEC’s handling of the ADC leadership dispute. National Commissioner Mohammed Haruna told The PUNCH that INEC had been served notice of the appeal and would await the appellate court’s decision before determining its next course of action. The rival Nafiu Gombe-led faction continues pressing for implementation of the Federal High Court judgment. That reported administrative position offers greater clarity. It does not amount to an appellate victory for the Mark-led leadership. A separate ruling today also requires precision. The Federal High Court rejected Atiku and the ADC’s application to amend their suit challenging Tinubu’s eligibility. The judge directed the parties to proceed with the substantive case. The ruling on the amendment should therefore not be described as a final determination of the underlying eligibility dispute. For the ADC, the practical challenge remains sustaining a nationwide campaign while litigation demands attention and resources. The Technology Debate Needs Answers Atiku has asked INEC to permit independent scrutiny of its proposed use of artificial intelligence in processing polling-unit results. His petition seeks disclosure, audit arrangements and clear procedures for reviewing results flagged by the system. The demand raises questions that deserve public answers. It does not establish that manipulation has occurred. INEC should explain what the proposed technology does, where human decisions enter the process and how errors would be challenged and corrected. The approaching November 28 mock exercise gives those explanations urgency. Public confidence would benefit from published test findings and an account of any corrective work required. A successful demonstration should allow parties, observers and citizens to understand how the system behaves when something goes wrong, as well as when it works. State Police: A Reform With Electoral Weight Security reform has also advanced. Reporting this week says the state police constitutional alteration bill has been transmitted for presidential assent, while a separate operational framework remains necessary. This is politically consequential because security is both a public demand and a question of institutional power. Supporters see the prospect of policing closer to communities. Concerns about governors’ influence make safeguards central to the proposal’s credibility. The campaign debate should examine funding, appointments, complaints, oversight and protection against partisan deployment. Passage of a reform and the creation of an effective service are distinct milestones. What Changed This Week? APC/Tinubu: The Anambra gathering reinforced the cross-party campaign strategy. Its value depends on whether APGA’s organisation and Soludo’s advocacy persuade additional presidential voters. NDC/Obi-Kwankwaso: Friday’s Onitsha activity demonstrated mobilisation in Obi’s home state. National viability still depends on reach, organisation and turnout beyond familiar strongholds. ADC/Atiku: INEC’s reported decision to await the appeal provides administrative clarity, while the underlying legal uncertainty continues. APM/Makinde and other opposition partners: The revised summit date preserves the cooperation process but compresses the time available to implement any agreement. The competitive position cannot responsibly be reduced to rally photographs, endorsements or partisan state-by-state predictions. No fresh, credible national polling reviewed for this edition establishes a decisive swing. Recent local and off-cycle contests remain useful indicators when assessed alongside turnout, competitiveness and local circumstances. Their results should inform presidential analysis without becoming automatic forecasts. item.title: Was Vladimir Putin 'snubbed' by Xi Jinping? Viral handshake video is AI fake
item.description: A viral video appearing to show China's Xi Jinping "snubbing" Vladimir Putin at the APEC summit has racked up millions of views, fuelling speculation about tensions between Beijing and Moscow. But the footage is fake. FRANCE 24 traced the original video to an earlier summit, where the two leaders did shake hands. The creator, who runs a satire account, admitted to manipulating the footage using Grok Imagine, an AI tool developed by Elon Musk's xAI, as Vedika Bahl explains.

item.title: Young Protesters Hit Streets Across Europe
item.description: Protesters rallied across Europe on Friday to vent anger over issues from high living costs to military spending and the climate crisis, ramping up pressure on political leaders they accuse of ignoring the concerns of young people. Demonstrators hit the streets in cities from Italy to Germany, Switzerland and Britain, many waving signs emblazoned with “fight for our future”, setting off flares and burning cardboard models of tanks. The rallies, coordinated by a youth-led coalition of over 50 groups, are fuelled by grievances that vary from place to place, including Israel’s war in Gaza, high rents and deteriorating learning conditions at schools and universities. But a common theme runs through them — a sense that governments across the continent are too busy with geopolitical crises and helping big business, and not investing enough in the well-being of younger generations. Olivia Ferrario, an 18-year-old high school student at a protest in the Italian city of Milan, told AFP that young people were displaying their “dynamism and determination” by taking to the streets. “If the government does not listen to us, we cannot remain silent,” she said at the demonstration that attracted tens of thousands of protesters. Police deployed in large numbers due to fears of a repeat of the street violence that has marred recent major protests in France and other countries. Protesters dressed up as clowns jump during a youth demonstration under the motto “Stop ReArm Europe!” ‘Lost So Much Hope’ In Switzerland, organisers claimed that more than 40,000 protesters had taken to the streets nationwide. “Austerity is social violence,” read a banner in Lausanne, while another blared: “Be vegan, but eat the rich.” The demonstrations were mostly peaceful. But a small number of people clashed with police after it ended, resulting in the deployment of tear gas and water cannon, the domestic Keystone-ATS news agency reported. In Berlin, about 1,000 university students and school pupils protested over concerns including Germany’s rapid rearmament, which has stoked fears of a return to compulsory military service. “I simply think it’s indefensible… to force someone to learn how to fight and kill, and then send them to war,” Helena Kossatz, 18, who finished high school last year, told AFP. While Europe seeks to rearm in the face of a hostile Russia, organisers of the continent-wide protests say funds allocated to rearmament should be spent on education, youth policies and housing. Several hundred protesters, some in school uniform, gathered at demonstrations in London outside parliament and in nearby Trafalgar Square, waving placards that said “save higher education” and “Fight for our futures not their wars”. “I’ve lost so much hope,” Eliz, who had taken the day off from college and gave only one name, told AFP. item.content:encoded: Protesters rallied across Europe on Friday to vent anger over issues from high living costs to military spending and the climate crisis, ramping up pressure on political leaders they accuse of ignoring the concerns of young people. Demonstrators hit the streets in cities from Italy to Germany, Switzerland and Britain, many waving signs emblazoned with “fight for our future”, setting off flares and burning cardboard models of tanks. The rallies, coordinated by a youth-led coalition of over 50 groups, are fuelled by grievances that vary from place to place, including Israel’s war in Gaza, high rents and deteriorating learning conditions at schools and universities. But a common theme runs through them — a sense that governments across the continent are too busy with geopolitical crises and helping big business, and not investing enough in the well-being of younger generations. Olivia Ferrario, an 18-year-old high school student at a protest in the Italian city of Milan, told AFP that young people were displaying their “dynamism and determination” by taking to the streets. “If the government does not listen to us, we cannot remain silent,” she said at the demonstration that attracted tens of thousands of protesters. Police deployed in large numbers due to fears of a repeat of the street violence that has marred recent major protests in France and other countries. Protesters dressed up as clowns jump during a youth demonstration under the motto “Stop ReArm Europe!” ‘Lost So Much Hope’ In Switzerland, organisers claimed that more than 40,000 protesters had taken to the streets nationwide. “Austerity is social violence,” read a banner in Lausanne, while another blared: “Be vegan, but eat the rich.” The demonstrations were mostly peaceful. But a small number of people clashed with police after it ended, resulting in the deployment of tear gas and water cannon, the domestic Keystone-ATS news agency reported. In Berlin, about 1,000 university students and school pupils protested over concerns including Germany’s rapid rearmament, which has stoked fears of a return to compulsory military service. “I simply think it’s indefensible… to force someone to learn how to fight and kill, and then send them to war,” Helena Kossatz, 18, who finished high school last year, told AFP. While Europe seeks to rearm in the face of a hostile Russia, organisers of the continent-wide protests say funds allocated to rearmament should be spent on education, youth policies and housing. Several hundred protesters, some in school uniform, gathered at demonstrations in London outside parliament and in nearby Trafalgar Square, waving placards that said “save higher education” and “Fight for our futures not their wars”. “I’ve lost so much hope,” Eliz, who had taken the day off from college and gave only one name, told AFP. The 18-year-old said she was unsure whether she would go to university, “because of money. Because most jobs are getting taken over by AI. Everyone’s just kind of more depressed”. There were scuffles between groups of right-wing and anti-fascist demonstrators, and AFP saw a handful of arrests. Chants of “Palestine will live forever” rang out at the London protests, and Palestinian flags were on display at several of the demonstrations across Europe. In Rome, high school students marched behind a banner that read: “We will take freedom if no one gives it to us — against the government, the war and the high cost of living.” There were scuffles in the Italian capital, with some protesters throwing bottles and smoke bombs at police. Protesters face police officers wearing white helmets during a demonstration organised by “GenZ regelt!” ‘Dreadful’ Schools Demonstrators called for more funding for education and railed against increased military spending during protests in the Spanish capital Madrid. Gabriela Gimeno Serrano, a 16-year-old high school student, said there were 33 students in her class with just one teacher. “Classrooms are very small, the facilities are in an absolutely dreadful state,” she told AFP, adding some schools were even plagued by rats and cockroaches. Protests are set to extend into the weekend, with trade unions and housing associations calling for further demonstrations. The protests come around the anniversary of the Yellow Vests movement in France, which rattled President Emmanuel Macron in 2018 and 2019. Demonstrations are planned there on Saturday. The protests in European countries have in part been inspired by recent demonstrations in France, which have sometimes turned violent. Those began when students demonstrated at high schools in mid-September to demand better learning conditions, fuelling a nationwide campaign against soaring prices, inadequate public services and police brutality. item.title: 10th anniversary: Oba Ewuare II’s reign strengthens traditional institution — Sultan
item.description: The Sultan of Sokoto, Alhaji Muhammad Sa’ad Abubakar, has congratulated the Oba of Benin, Oba Ewuare II, on his 10th coronation anniversary, commending his leadership and commitment to cultural preservation, peacebuilding and national unity. The Sultan described the anniversary as a significant milestone marking a decade of traditional leadership and dedication to the progress and well-being of the Benin Kingdom and its people. In a statement issued on Saturday by Prince Bashir Adefaka, for the Sultan’s Media Team, Abubakar praised the monarch for upholding the cultural heritage, traditions and historical identity of the Benin Kingdom. He also commended Oba Ewuare II for promoting peaceful coexistence, mutual respect and unity among Nigerians across ethnic, religious and cultural divides. The Sultan noted that traditional institutions remained indispensable to national cohesion, the promotion of moral values, community development and peaceful coexistence, particularly at a time when Nigeria needed the collective wisdom and leadership of traditional rulers to address its challenges. He said the Oba’s 10-year reign had reinforced the importance of traditional institutions as custodians of history, culture, values and the aspirations of their people. According to him, the Benin monarch has also continued to serve as a rallying point for unity, stability and development. Abubakar, who is physically present in Benin City for the anniversary celebration, expressed delight at being part of the historic occasion. He said his presence demonstrated the enduring bonds of brotherhood, friendship and mutual respect among traditional rulers in Nigeria, irrespective of ethnic and regional differences. The Sultan prayed for continued good health, wisdom, strength and long life for Oba Ewuare II, urging divine guidance for the monarch as he leads the Benin Kingdom towards greater peace, prosperity and development. He also prayed for sustained peace and progress in the Benin Kingdom, Edo State and Nigeria. The post 10th anniversary: Oba Ewuare II’s reign strengthens traditional institution — Sultan appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: George R.R. Martin’s 7 Best Non-Game of Thrones Books, Ranked
item.description: George R.R. Martin will forever be associated with his book series, A Song of Ice and Fire , and HBO’s adaptation, Game of Thrones , but there's considerably more to his bibliography than scheming Lannisters, fire-breathing dragons, and the unending wait for The Winds of Winter . Long before Westeros became a cultural phenomenon, Martin was building a reputation as one of science fiction and fantasy's most imaginative voices, writing everything from supernatural mysteries and vampiric thrillers to sprawling space operas and intimate character dramas.

item.title: HURIWA mourns Vanguard Online Editor, Femi Ajasa
item.description: The Human Rights Writers Association of Nigeria (HURIWA) has mourned the death of Vanguard Online Editor, Olufemi Finayon Ajasa, describing his passing at the age of 44 as a major loss to the journalism profession and Nigeria’s media industry. Ajasa reportedly died following a brief illness. In a condolence statement issued on Thursday, November 19, 2026, HURIWA’s National Coordinator, Comrade Emmanuel Nnadozie Onwubiko, said the journalist died at a time when his experience, creativity and digital expertise were still needed in the media industry. The association described his death as particularly painful, noting that he belonged to a generation of journalists who successfully combined traditional journalistic values with the demands of digital journalism, online storytelling and editorial management. HURIWA said Ajasa’s professional career began in photojournalism at National Mirror before he moved into editorial and digital leadership roles at Vanguard, TheNewsGuru and Pulse. It described his career progression as a reflection of his dedication, versatility and commitment to the development of Nigerian journalism. The association noted that his return to Vanguard in 2022 as Online Editor demonstrated the confidence reposed in his professional competence, experience and ability to contribute to newsroom development. HURIWA extended its condolences to the management and staff of Vanguard Media Limited, the Ajasa family, friends, colleagues and professional associates, urging them to draw strength from the positive impact he made during his lifetime. The association also drew attention to the pressures and emotional demands of journalism, noting that media professionals often work under intense deadlines and challenging circumstances to keep the public informed. While acknowledging that words might not adequately ease the pain of his loss, HURIWA urged the bereaved family to take solace in the legacy Ajasa left behind and the lives he touched through his professional and personal relationships. The association prayed for the peaceful repose of his soul and asked God to grant his family, Vanguard management and the journalism community the strength to bear the loss. The post HURIWA mourns Vanguard Online Editor, Femi Ajasa appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Russian projectiles hit Poland as NATO tensions rise
item.description: Three Russian projectiles came down in Poland on Friday, prompting NATO to condemn what it called a grave violation of Polish airspace. A suspected jet-powered drone and a missile struck separate locations near the Ukrainian border, while another missile crashed just 35 kilometres from an area where European troops are taking part in military exercises. Meanwhile, troops from eight NATO countries are conducting drills in neighbouring Lithuania. With US-led peace talks yet to make a breakthrough, tensions between Europe and Russia remain high. Peter O’Brien reports.

item.title: EU, UK reach reset deal after Brexit
item.description: The UK and the EU signed three agreements on Friday at a summit in Brussels, marking a new effort to reset post-Brexit relations. The deals aim to reduce red tape for food exports, link emissions trading schemes and allow tens of thousands of young people to live and work more freely across the Channel. Prime Minister Andy Burnham has called Brexit an “obvious failure” to deliver on its promises and wants to deepen ties with the EU, a position criticised by veteran Brexiteer Nigel Farage, who has warned of a political backlash. Daniel Quinlan has this story.

item.title: Why Nigeria is seeking stronger EU partnership to combat terrorism – Defence Minister
item.description: Reveals Troops Intercepted Over 400 Starlinks Devices Linked to Terrorist Networks. By: Kingsley Omonobi The Minister of Defence, General Christopher Gwabin Musa (rtd), has reaffirmed the Federal Government’s commitment to a comprehensive, whole-of-government strategy to combat terrorism, while seeking stronger security cooperation with the European Union (EU). Musa made this known at the third edition of the Schuman Security and Defence Forum held at the European Parliament in Brussels, Belgium, where he represented Nigeria. Disclosing that the Armed Forces of Nigeria were deploying intelligence-led operations, advanced surveillance systems, unmanned aerial platforms and military artificial intelligence to weaken terrorist networks, the Minister told the gathering that troops of Operation Hadin Kai intercepted more than 400 Starlink communication devices linked to terrorist networks in the North-East in May 2026. A statement issued by the Special Adviser on Media to the Minister, Leah Katung-Babatunde quoted the minister saying Nigeria was shifting from a predominantly military approach to a coordinated counterterrorism strategy involving intelligence gathering, law enforcement, community engagement and socio-economic interventions. He explained that terrorism remained a complex security challenge fuelled by economic vulnerabilities, porous borders, local grievances and transnational organised crime. The minister said the strategy, guided by Nigeria’s National Counter Terrorism Strategy (NACTEST), reflected the administration’s determination to address both the immediate threats posed by terrorist groups and the underlying factors sustaining insecurity. Addressing the growing use of emerging technologies by violent extremist groups, Musa highlighted Nigeria’s efforts to counter the illicit deployment of drones, digital communication devices and satellite technologies. He said the Armed Forces of Nigeria were deploying intelligence-led operations, advanced surveillance systems, unmanned aerial platforms and military artificial intelligence to weaken terrorist networks. He particularly disclosed that troops of Operation Hadin Kai intercepted more than 400 Starlink communication devices linked to terrorist networks in the North-East in May 2026. Musa also highlighted the Ministry of Defence’s efforts to promote indigenous defence innovation through research and partnerships with the private sector. He called for stronger collaboration with the European Union in counter-drone technologies, digital forensics and satellite intelligence to enhance Nigeria’s capacity to respond to evolving security threats. On the financial networks sustaining terrorism, the minister stressed the need to dismantle criminal economies, including kidnapping for ransom, illegal mining, cattle rustling and illicit arms trafficking. item.content:encoded: Reveals Troops Intercepted Over 400 Starlinks Devices Linked to Terrorist Networks. By: Kingsley Omonobi The Minister of Defence, General Christopher Gwabin Musa (rtd), has reaffirmed the Federal Government’s commitment to a comprehensive, whole-of-government strategy to combat terrorism, while seeking stronger security cooperation with the European Union (EU). Musa made this known at the third edition of the Schuman Security and Defence Forum held at the European Parliament in Brussels, Belgium, where he represented Nigeria. Disclosing that the Armed Forces of Nigeria were deploying intelligence-led operations, advanced surveillance systems, unmanned aerial platforms and military artificial intelligence to weaken terrorist networks, the Minister told the gathering that troops of Operation Hadin Kai intercepted more than 400 Starlink communication devices linked to terrorist networks in the North-East in May 2026. A statement issued by the Special Adviser on Media to the Minister, Leah Katung-Babatunde quoted the minister saying Nigeria was shifting from a predominantly military approach to a coordinated counterterrorism strategy involving intelligence gathering, law enforcement, community engagement and socio-economic interventions. He explained that terrorism remained a complex security challenge fuelled by economic vulnerabilities, porous borders, local grievances and transnational organised crime. The minister said the strategy, guided by Nigeria’s National Counter Terrorism Strategy (NACTEST), reflected the administration’s determination to address both the immediate threats posed by terrorist groups and the underlying factors sustaining insecurity. Addressing the growing use of emerging technologies by violent extremist groups, Musa highlighted Nigeria’s efforts to counter the illicit deployment of drones, digital communication devices and satellite technologies. He said the Armed Forces of Nigeria were deploying intelligence-led operations, advanced surveillance systems, unmanned aerial platforms and military artificial intelligence to weaken terrorist networks. He particularly disclosed that troops of Operation Hadin Kai intercepted more than 400 Starlink communication devices linked to terrorist networks in the North-East in May 2026. Musa also highlighted the Ministry of Defence’s efforts to promote indigenous defence innovation through research and partnerships with the private sector. He called for stronger collaboration with the European Union in counter-drone technologies, digital forensics and satellite intelligence to enhance Nigeria’s capacity to respond to evolving security threats. On the financial networks sustaining terrorism, the minister stressed the need to dismantle criminal economies, including kidnapping for ransom, illegal mining, cattle rustling and illicit arms trafficking. He said the Nigerian Financial Intelligence Unit (NFIU), National Counter Terrorism Centre (NCTC) and other security agencies were working together to trace illicit financial flows, prosecute criminal facilitators and strengthen border security to disrupt terrorist supply chains. The Defence minister further reaffirmed Nigeria’s commitment to regional and international security cooperation through the Multinational Joint Task Force (MNJTF) in the Lake Chad Basin, the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS), the African Union and the West Africa Police Information Systems (WAPIS) He also emphasised that the Armed Forces remained committed to operating within the framework of national laws and international humanitarian law, with priority given to civilian protection and due process in the prosecution of suspects. According to him, Nigeria also recognises the importance of rehabilitation and reintegration programmes for eligible former combatants through initiatives such as Operation Safe Corridor. The Schuman Security and Defence Forum provides a platform for high-level discussions on international peace, security and defence among defence ministers of partner countries, European Union member states, representatives of international organisations and leading think tanks. item.title: Sultan arrives Benin to honour Oba Ewuare II on 10th coronation anniversary
item.description: The Sultan of Sokoto, His Eminence Alhaji Muhammad Sa’ad Abubakar, has arrived Benin City, Edo State, ahead of the 10th coronation anniversary of the Oba of Benin, Omo N’Oba N’Edo, Uku Akpolokpolo, Oba Ewuare II, Oba of Benin. The aircraft conveying the Sultan touched ground at the Oba Akenzua II Airport in the Edo State capital 25 minutes after departing the Samuel Ladoke Akintola International Airport, Ibadan, Oyo State, at 5:05 p.m. on Friday, November 20. In a statement by Prince Bashir Adefaka on behalf of the Media Team of the Sultan of Sokoto, noted that the Sultan was received by senior members of the Oba of Benin-in-Council at the airport. He was accompanied on the flight by the Galadiman Gerin Sokoto, His Royal Highness Alhaji Aliyu Attahiru Galadanci, and former Director-General, National Broadcasting Commission, NBC, Mallam Danladi Bako, Kogunan Sokoto. The Sultan arrived Ibadan on a weeklong South-West working visit on Sunday, November 15, starting off his activities with participation in the 11th General Assembly of the Muslim Ummah of South West Nigeria, MUSWEN, as special guest of honour. The Sultan also performed his duty as Chancellor of the University of Ibadan on Tuesday, November 17, supported by his Pro-Chancellor and Chairman Governing Council, Chief Bisi Akande, as well as the new Vice-Chancellor, Professor Peter Olamakinde Olapegba, among others. On Wednesday, he travelled from his Ibadan to Saki to partake – as Chairman of the Day – in the official commissioning of the 500-seat Alhaji Azeez Adedokun Olowolagba Information and Communication Technology, ICT, Centre built and donated to the College of Nursing Sciences, Muslim Medical Foundation Saki, by Alhaji Mudasiru Adedokun Olowolagba, in memory of his late father. On Thursday, the Sultan paid a courtesy call on the Aseyin of Iseyin, Oba Sefiu Olawale Adeyemi III (Ajirotutu I), who will be celebrating his third coronation anniversary on December 11. He also witnessed the award ceremony by the Iseyin Kingdom in honour of legal luminary and philanthropist, Barrister Ahmed Raji (SAN). On Friday, the Sultan of Sokoto paid a courtesy visit to the palace of the Olubadan of Ibadan Land, where Oba Rashidi Ladoja, Arusa I, assisted by Olubadan-in-Council, received him. Both monarchs then proceeded to the Bodija Muslim Community Central Mosque, Ibadan, where they observed their Jumat service led by the Chief Imam, Sheikh Hakeem Ibrahim. He the left for Benin City, where he was first received by members of the Oba of Benin-in-Council and then later by the royal host himself in his palace the same Friday night. Vanguard News The post Sultan arrives Benin to honour Oba Ewuare II on 10th coronation anniversary appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Countries race to secure COP31 deal after fossil fuel row
item.description: The COP31 climate talks spilled into Saturday as countries raced to secure a deal after a draft text dropped all mention of fossil fuels, exposing deep divisions over how to tackle global warming. Nearly 200 nations remained deadlocked after two weeks of grinding UN talks in Turkey, with negotiators working through the night after missing their scheduled Friday finish amid feuds over energy, science and finance. Australia, which is presiding over the COP31 negotiations, raced against the clock to produce a third draft deal, with many delegates due to catch flights home. “We are close to the finish line, but we are not there yet,” COP31 President Murat Kurum, who is Turkey’s environment minister, told an assembly late Friday that approved some technical matters. Midway through his opening address, Kurum was forced to pause while a protester shouted “You are killing the future!” before being escorted from the hall. Expectations of a major breakthrough have been low at COP31 as countries grapple with an oil price shock and geopolitical tensions stemming from the war in Iran. The summit follows a string of climate-linked disasters from Europe to Nepal and Indonesia and unfolds as a super El Nino pattern amplifies the risk of further extreme weather. A draft deal unveiled earlier this week called for a faster phase-out of fossil fuels, a flashpoint at UN climate talks where producers such as Saudi Arabia have fiercely resisted such calls. A second, pared-down draft released on Thursday stripped away all mentions of fossil fuels — sending negotiators rushing back to the bargaining table. The European Union said the revised draft “risks turning this climate COP into a fossil summit”. A dozen European and developing countries — from France to Panama and the Solomon Islands — released a letter Friday insisting that the deal include “a clear transition away from fossil fuels”. Panama, which also signed the letter, threatened to walk away from the talks. The country’s environment minister, Juan Carlos Navarro, is a vocal critic of the climate negotiations, accusing a “petroleum mafia” of blocking progress. Meanwhile, the OPEC oil cartel wrote on X that its head, Haitham Al Ghais, met Russian presidential climate envoy Ruslan Edelgeriev at COP31 to discuss “the importance of inclusive and balanced approaches across all multilateral environmental fora”. – ‘Clean electrification’ – Australia’s Climate Minister Chris Bowen, who shuttled between delegations to seek compromises, said Friday he would work “for as long as it takes, to get the job done”. The draft “cover decision” proposes a target to electrify the global economy — a push to replace technologies that burn fossil fuels directly, like diesel cars and gas heating, with electric alternatives. item.dc:creator: Ayobami
item.content:encoded: The COP31 climate talks spilled into Saturday as countries raced to secure a deal after a draft text dropped all mention of fossil fuels, exposing deep divisions over how to tackle global warming. Nearly 200 nations remained deadlocked after two weeks of grinding UN talks in Turkey, with negotiators working through the night after missing their scheduled Friday finish amid feuds over energy, science and finance. Australia, which is presiding over the COP31 negotiations, raced against the clock to produce a third draft deal, with many delegates due to catch flights home. “We are close to the finish line, but we are not there yet,” COP31 President Murat Kurum, who is Turkey’s environment minister, told an assembly late Friday that approved some technical matters. Midway through his opening address, Kurum was forced to pause while a protester shouted “You are killing the future!” before being escorted from the hall. Expectations of a major breakthrough have been low at COP31 as countries grapple with an oil price shock and geopolitical tensions stemming from the war in Iran. The summit follows a string of climate-linked disasters from Europe to Nepal and Indonesia and unfolds as a super El Nino pattern amplifies the risk of further extreme weather. A draft deal unveiled earlier this week called for a faster phase-out of fossil fuels, a flashpoint at UN climate talks where producers such as Saudi Arabia have fiercely resisted such calls. A second, pared-down draft released on Thursday stripped away all mentions of fossil fuels — sending negotiators rushing back to the bargaining table. The European Union said the revised draft “risks turning this climate COP into a fossil summit”. A dozen European and developing countries — from France to Panama and the Solomon Islands — released a letter Friday insisting that the deal include “a clear transition away from fossil fuels”. Panama, which also signed the letter, threatened to walk away from the talks. The country’s environment minister, Juan Carlos Navarro, is a vocal critic of the climate negotiations, accusing a “petroleum mafia” of blocking progress. Meanwhile, the OPEC oil cartel wrote on X that its head, Haitham Al Ghais, met Russian presidential climate envoy Ruslan Edelgeriev at COP31 to discuss “the importance of inclusive and balanced approaches across all multilateral environmental fora”. – ‘Clean electrification’ – Australia’s Climate Minister Chris Bowen, who shuttled between delegations to seek compromises, said Friday he would work “for as long as it takes, to get the job done”. The draft “cover decision” proposes a target to electrify the global economy — a push to replace technologies that burn fossil fuels directly, like diesel cars and gas heating, with electric alternatives. The goal is championed by COP31 hosts Turkey and Australia, who tout “electrification” as integral to tackling concerns over energy security and sluggish global progress in cutting heat-trapping emissions. “Electrification is the key to transitioning away from fossil fuels,” said Bowen, who is chairing the negotiations. The proposal calls for countries to boost the global share of final energy demand met by electricity to 35 percent by 2035. But it does not specify that the additional electricity must come from renewables rather than coal or gas, spurring some countries to demand an explicitly “clean” target. Some countries also rejected a proposal to ramp up carbon capture, dismissing it as a costly, unproven technology that could allow polluters to keep burning fossil fuels. – $120 billion target – Countries are sharply divided over a raft of other issues. The timing of the next set of reports by the UN’s Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) has been a major source of friction. The latest draft expressed “deep concern” over the imminent breach of the 1.5C goal but dropped an earlier call to return warming below that threshold as soon as possible this century. Negotiations are also deadlocked over long-running complaints by developing countries that rich nations are falling short in their obligations to help them confront climate change. The removal of a $120 billion target for climate adaptation angered developing nations. “We didn’t come here to beg,” said Ghana’s environment minister, Zanetor Agyeman-Rawlings. item.title: Gary Larson's 10 Greatest 'Far Side' Comics, Ranked
item.description: What, exactly, is the measure of greatness when it comes to comic strips ? The daily newspaper comic is a very limiting art form, with only a few panels — sometimes just one panel — to make a joke. Because of its brevity, it's easy to trivialize the medium as simply the “funny papers,” a daily, disposable art form designed to pick you up after reading the actual news.

item.title: Goodbye 'Rings of Power,' Prime Video’s Legendary 48-Episode Fantasy Series Is Even Better
item.description: Rings of Power is back on Prime Video for a third helping of fantasy storytelling, and we won’t pretend we aren’t enamored with all the shenanigans happening in Middle-earth right now. Still, considering how much Amazon has spent on the series (and how incoherent parts of the story can be), we’re not convinced it's the streamer’s best fantasy show. In our minds, that honor belongs to another.

item.title: 2027: INEC REC seeks traditional rulers’ support for peaceful, secure elections in Benue
item.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC) in Benue State, Mallam Aminu Idris, has called on traditional rulers in the state to promote a peaceful and secure environment before and during the 2027 general elections. Idris made the appeal during a courtesy visit to the Tor Tiv and Chairman of the Benue State Council of Traditional Rulers, His Royal Majesty, Orcivirigh Prof. James Ayatse, on Friday, November 20, 2026, as part of the Commission’s stakeholder engagement ahead of the elections. The REC also solicited the support of the traditional institution in encouraging eligible voters to collect their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) and strengthening collaboration with INEC to ensure successful conduct of the forthcoming polls. According to a statement by the Public Affairs Officer of INEC in Benue State, Mrs. Peace Ogoyi, Idris described the visit as a vital step in the Commission’s preparations for the 2027 elections. “He solicited the intervention and support of the royal father in three key areas: encouraging the collection of Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs), promoting a peaceful and secure environment before and during the elections, and providing further support to the Commission through sustained collaboration.” Responding, the Tor Tiv welcomed the REC and his delegation, expressing appreciation for the visit and acknowledging the important role of traditional rulers in ensuring a conducive environment for electoral activities. He noted that “traditional rulers, as fathers of the state, have a responsibility to receive electoral officials and ensure their safety and provision of a peaceful working environment. Drawing from his experience in previous elections, including his service in various ad hoc capacities and as a State Returning Officer, Ayatse acknowledged the enormous responsibilities confronting the Commission. He said the Traditional Council had consistently advocated peaceful political campaigns and a level playing field for all political parties. The monarch further disclosed that traditional and religious leaders had organised prayers for peaceful elections and maintained constructive engagements with security agencies to strengthen peace and security across the state. He assured the REC that the Council would continue to collaborate with relevant stakeholders to identify and address electoral security flashpoints ahead of the elections. On the credibility of the electoral process, the Tor Tiv emphasised the need for INEC to uphold the will of the people, urging the Commission’s personnel to discharge their duties with neutrality, fairness and professionalism. He noted that “traditional rulers, as fathers of the state, have a responsibility to receive electoral officials and ensure their safety and provision of a peaceful working environment. Drawing from his experience in previous elections, including his service in various ad hoc capacities and as a State Returning Officer, Ayatse acknowledged the enormous responsibilities confronting the Commission. He said the Traditional Council had consistently advocated peaceful political campaigns and a level playing field for all political parties. The monarch further disclosed that traditional and religious leaders had organised prayers for peaceful elections and maintained constructive engagements with security agencies to strengthen peace and security across the state. According to him, PVC collection and participation in elections are shared responsibilities that require the collective efforts of all stakeholders. The Tor Tiv offered prayers for peaceful, successful and outstanding elections in the state. The Benue INEC Administrative Secretary, Mr. Shikfu Bewaran, appreciated the monarch for the warm reception accorded the INEC delegation, describing the Tor Tiv as not only a father to the state but also a traditional ruler with practical experience and a deep understanding of the electoral process. item.title: Obi best hope for Nigerians, NDC chairman Cleopas declares
item.description: …Says 2027 poll must be referendum on Tinubu’s performance By Emem Idio, Yenagoa The National Chairman of the Nigeria Democratic Congress ,NDC, Senator Moses Cleopas, has described the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, as the best hope for Nigerians, urging the electorate to vote out the President Bola Tinubu-led administration in the 2027 general election. Cleopas said the country could not afford another four years under an administration that, in his assessment, had failed to address the worsening economic hardship, insecurity and rising cost of living. He described the 2027 presidential election as an opportunity for Nigerians to determine the future direction of the country and hold the incumbent government accountable for its performance. The former senator representing Bayelsa Central made the remarks on Friday in Yenagoa during a celebration marking his 57th birthday. He said the election should serve as a referendum on the Tinubu administration, arguing that a second-term mandate must be earned through demonstrable performance rather than political sentiment. “Second-term election is a referendum. It is standing on the leg of your previous performance. If you have done well, they give you another mandate. If you have not done well, they ask you to go home,” he said. Cleopas said the impact of the economic crisis was being felt by families across the country, including his own, citing complaints from his wife and children about the rising cost of household upkeep and education. He urged voters to assess the presidential candidates on the basis of competence, track record and their capacity to address the country’s problems, rather than party loyalty, religious considerations or financial inducements. The NDC chairman expressed confidence that Obi would win the 2027 presidential election, insisting that his candidacy offered Nigerians a credible alternative to the present administration. On insecurity, Cleopas condemned the persistent killings and abductions across the country, particularly attacks involving schoolchildren, accusing the government of failing in its fundamental responsibility to protect lives and property. Recounting his experience in the Senate, he said lawmakers from different parts of northern Nigeria frequently reported killings in their constituencies, including the deaths of women and children. He argued that insecurity should concern every Nigerian, irrespective of where attacks occurred, warning against the tendency to treat violence as a distant problem until it reaches one’s community. Ahead of the 2027 elections, Cleopas accused some politicians of deploying money and public resources to weaken opposition parties and influence voters. He specifically criticised an alleged plan by a political figure in Bayelsa to offer N50,000 per vote, describing the proposal as an affront to the electorate. Cleopas said the country could not afford another four years under an administration that, in his assessment, had failed to address the worsening economic hardship, insecurity and rising cost of living. He described the 2027 presidential election as an opportunity for Nigerians to determine the future direction of the country and hold the incumbent government accountable for its performance. The former senator representing Bayelsa Central made the remarks on Friday in Yenagoa during a celebration marking his 57th birthday. He said the election should serve as a referendum on the Tinubu administration, arguing that a second-term mandate must be earned through demonstrable performance rather than political sentiment. “Second-term election is a referendum. It is standing on the leg of your previous performance. If you have done well, they give you another mandate. If you have not done well, they ask you to go home,” he said. Cleopas said the impact of the economic crisis was being felt by families across the country, including his own, citing complaints from his wife and children about the rising cost of household upkeep and education. He urged voters to assess the presidential candidates on the basis of competence, track record and their capacity to address the country’s problems, rather than party loyalty, religious considerations or financial inducements. The NDC chairman expressed confidence that Obi would win the 2027 presidential election, insisting that his candidacy offered Nigerians a credible alternative to the present administration. On insecurity, Cleopas condemned the persistent killings and abductions across the country, particularly attacks involving schoolchildren, accusing the government of failing in its fundamental responsibility to protect lives and property. Recounting his experience in the Senate, he said lawmakers from different parts of northern Nigeria frequently reported killings in their constituencies, including the deaths of women and children. He argued that insecurity should concern every Nigerian, irrespective of where attacks occurred, warning against the tendency to treat violence as a distant problem until it reaches one’s community. Ahead of the 2027 elections, Cleopas accused some politicians of deploying money and public resources to weaken opposition parties and influence voters. He specifically criticised an alleged plan by a political figure in Bayelsa to offer N50,000 per vote, describing the proposal as an affront to the electorate. The former lawmaker warned public office holders against using government resources for partisan political activities, insisting that those entrusted with public funds must be held accountable for their use. On the NDC’s prospects in Bayelsa, Cleopas expressed confidence that the party would make significant electoral gains, citing what he described as growing support among young people. He, however, ruled out violence as a means of pursuing political power, urging the state government to guarantee the safety of opposition politicians and their supporters and ensure a level playing field for all parties. “Violence is not part of constitutional democracy. It is alien to democracy. It is the responsibility of the ruling government to provide security,” he said. Cleopas said opposition parties were entitled to equal protection under the law, disclosing that the NDC had adopted the practice of formally notifying security agencies and other relevant authorities ahead of its political activities. He also accused the ruling party of deliberately organising rival political events in communities whenever the NDC scheduled campaigns or other political engagements, alleging that the tactic was intended to disrupt the opposition’s activities. He called on Nigerians, regardless of political affiliation, to participate actively in the 2027 elections, mobilise their families and resist attempts to buy their votes. item.title: NASA Mars rover and orbiter suffer glitches
item.description: It's been a bad few weeks for technology on and off the planet, as NASA reported problems with its Perseverance Mars rover and Odyssey orbiter this week. For Perseverance, the problem seems to be a relatively straightforward communications issue that has paused science operations because of low data rates. The Odyssey orbiter, however, is facing an issue that could end the mission. The 2001 Mars Odyssey reached orbit around Mars in October 2001 to search for evidence of water and ice on the surface. The mission was supposed to last two and a half years, but the spacecraft's operations have been extended for a quarter of a century. In that time, it has had its fair share of ups and downs, including the failure of one of its four reaction wheels in 2013. Three reaction wheels are needed to orient the spacecraft; otherwise, it must fall back to its hydrazine thrusters. Earlier in November, between the 4th and 6th, Odyssey dropped into safe mode, which engineers determined was caused by one of the remaining reaction wheels stopping spinning. Science data stopped flowing as the team worked to recover the component; the good news was that the wheel moved when commanded. The bad news is that if the thrusters need to be used, only a few months of fuel remain. More bad news is that the spacecraft is part of NASA's Mars Relay Network, and was responsible for sending back the first post-landing images from the Phoenix lander and the Spirit, Opportunity, and Curiosity rovers. Its loss (should it come to that) would therefore be keenly felt. In the event the orbiter is indeed approaching the end of the road, the European Space Agency's Mars Express (MEX) and Trace Gas Orbiter (TGO) could pick up some of the load although, as a former ESA insider put it: "MEX is a science mission that can do relay where TGO is a relay mission that also does science." According to NASA, TGO already sends the most relay data from Mars to Earth. The challenge facing the Perseverance trundlebot is one of communication. On October 30, the rover's main computer detected problems with the primary radio (a series of "heartbeats" from the device did not arrive as expected) and automatically switched to a redundant backup, placing itself in a protective safe mode. So far, so expected. Engineers brought the rover back from safe mode, analyzed the data, and made an unpleasant discovery. The backup radio was not performing as it should – it was operating at approximately half of its expected power output. Both radios were therefore deemed inoperable – at least until the team has got to the bottom of the issues – and the rover has used X-band communications over its high-gain antenna to talk to Earth ever since. The problem here is that the connection provides a significantly lower data rate, meaning science and instrument operations are on hold. Engineers are working first to return the backup radio to operational status, then to address the primary. ®

item.title: EFCC case: ‘I’m most vilified; I shall be vindicated’– Yahaya Bello
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Former Kogi State Governor Yahaya Bello has described himself as “the most transparent and the most vilified,” saying he expects to be vindicated over corruption allegations against him. Bello spoke on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Friday, saying he would not comment on the EFCC case in detail because it was before the courts. He said Kogi State’s budgets, audited accounts, and records of performance were available online and challenged journalists and others to examine them and ask questions under the Freedom of Information Act. “I’d rather decline to make a comment about EFCC on national television because we’re in court. However, from inception till date, all of our financials and budgets and the performance on the ground are online. We have our eight years’ budget, eight years’ final account, which we call an audited account, and the performance on the ground; we have them online,” he said. Bello said he had experience managing public resources before becoming governor and was already financially established. He said he granted local governments financial autonomy after taking office and left the allegations for the courts to determine. “I was never; I never assumed office as a poor man. I’m a man of my means before I assumed the office. God blessed me in my early age, and my children have been schooling in high-profile schools, both in Abuja and abroad. In any case, I don’t think I was a governor that time. The rest, I’ll leave it for them to prove it in court,” he said. He added, “I am the most transparent and the most vilified. I’m the most transparent. I’m the most vilified. But at the end of the day, I shall be vindicated.” Bello also said he had no regrets about his time as governor and accepted responsibility for what happened during his tenure, adding: “I gave my best.” The EFCC is prosecuting Bello in two separate cases relating to alleged financial misconduct during his 2016–2024 governorship tenure. The post EFCC case: ‘I’m most vilified; I shall be vindicated’– Yahaya Bello appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 11 dead, over 180 hospitalised after drinking alcohol
item.description: At least 11 people have died and more than 180 have been hospitalised after drinking suspected tainted alcohol in India’s northeastern state of Manipur. The victims fell ill after consuming the liquor, Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh said in a statement on Friday. “Over 180 patients have been admitted in the two hospitals so far, while the death toll has reached 11 in the last 48 hours,” the statement said. He also ordered an enquiry into the incident, saying those responsible would be arrested and punished. Deaths from illicit or adulterated alcohol are regularly reported in India, where cheap liquor sold outside regulated channels can contain methanol, a highly toxic industrial chemical. In May, at least 15 people died after drinking methanol-laced illicit liquor in Pune and neighbouring Pimpri-Chinchwad in the western state of Maharashtra. In August, 13 people died and more than 60 were affected after consuming methanol-tainted liquor in Gujarat’s Bhavnagar district, according to local media reports. Such liquor is widely consumed across India, where a bottle is sometimes sold for less than a dollar. If ingested, methanol can cause blindness, liver damage and death in larger concentrations. item.title: Four die, 24 rescued as Bayelsa burial boat capsizes
item.description: Four persons, including two children, have died after a boat conveying passengers to a burial ceremony capsized in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State on Friday. Twenty-four other passengers were rescued following the incident, which occurred at about 11am while the boat was travelling from Ayama community to Ukubie. The Bayelsa State Police Command said preliminary findings indicated that the boat developed a mechanical fault while navigating the waterways. The police spokesperson, Musa Mohammed, disclosed this in a statement on Friday, alleging that some passengers had urged the operator to steer towards the riverbank after the fault developed, but he declined and continued the journey before the boat capsized. Mohammed said the bodies of two adults and two children had been recovered and deposited at the mortuary of the Federal Medical Centre, Yenagoa. He said 24 survivors were rescued, with 19 taken to Ayama Clinic, while five others who sustained injuries were transferred to Family Care Hospital in Yenagoa for treatment. The police spokesperson disclosed that the boat operator, identified only as Omovie, had fled the scene, while the boat manager, identified as MV Bina, had been taken into custody for investigation. He added that the police marine section had been deployed to reinforce search and rescue operations, while the Divisional Police Officer in Oporoma was coordinating efforts with local divers and other emergency responders. Mohammed said investigations were ongoing to establish the circumstances surrounding the tragedy, assuring that search and rescue operations would continue until everyone on board had been accounted for.
